contract.settlement_definition: Binary contract on one named player: YES if he records 10 or more in two (double double) or three (triple double) of the five categories points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks in the single game named in the contract (floor_strike 0.5, strike_type greater). Inactive players, and active players who never take the court, settle at a fair price rather than NO; once the player enters the game the market settles on actual box-score statistics. A game postponed but starting within 48 hours stays open; cancelled or not started within 48 hours settles to a fair price. The rules sample is silent on whether overtime statistics count and the sample text is cut off before naming the source agency.

rules_evidence.quote: A double-double is achieved when a player reaches 10 or more in two of the five main statistical categories in a single game
rules_evidence.establishes: Defines the DD event as two of five categories (pts, reb, ast, stl, blk) at >=10 in one game.

rules_evidence.quote: If a player is inactive, or active but never takes the court, the market settles to a fair price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Participation voiding: only players who actually enter the game carry binary risk, so inactive-branch probability is irrelevant to the settled outcome.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player enters the game the market settles based on whether the player records a triple double.
rules_evidence.establishes: No protection against early exit: a player who enters and leaves after minutes settles on whatever he accumulated.

variants_and_edge_cases: Triple double (KXNBA3D) requires three categories at >=10; same five-category list, same voiding text, but a far thinner positive class dominated by a handful of high-assist bigs and guards, so base-rate shrinkage matters more than any matchup variable.
Steals and blocks are valid categories, so a rim protector can complete a DD with points+blocks or a TD with reb+blk; the common 'pts/reb/ast' simplification misses these paths.

Overtime is not mentioned in the sampled text; 'in a single game' on the official box score ordinarily includes OT minutes, which adds roughly 5 minutes to starters in ~6% of games and shifts DD probability materially for players at 8-9.

Inactive or never-entered player settles at a fair price (not NO), so unconditional participation modelling is unnecessary but the conditional-on-entering distribution needs a left tail for early exits.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official game box score as reported by the sports data sources named in the full rules; the sampled rules_secondary is truncated before naming them, so the exact source agency and stat-correction policy are unverified (see unresolved).

mechanism.summary: A double or triple double is a conjunction over counting categories, each of which is (minutes on court) x (per-minute opportunity rate) x (conversion), so the event is the upper tail of a jointly distributed vector with a common minutes factor. The chain is: does he enter and how long does he stay (scenario mixture: normal starter load, blowout cut, foul trouble, in-game exit, overtime), which teammates share the floor (which determines board and assist shares), how many possessions occur (pace), the per-category counts conditional on minutes with the right dependence structure (positive through minutes and pace, negative between a guard's scoring and passing), the discreteness of crossing exactly ten, and settlement by official box score. Because a rare binary event is driven by a few tail scenarios, scenario weights and the choice of category pair matter more than season-average per-game stats.

stages.name: Entry and early-exit truncation
stages.description: The market voids inactive or never-entered players, so participation only matters conditional on entering; but once he enters the contract settles on whatever he accumulates. The relevant first stage is therefore the probability mass on very short appearances: a questionable player on a minutes restriction, a player who rolls an ankle in the first quarter, an ejection or early foul-out. These branches deliver a near-zero chance of a DD and are priced as part of a normal game by anyone using average minutes.
stages.distribution: Mixture: majority mass at normal rotation minutes, a small discrete mass (a few percent, higher with injury designations) at under 15 minutes; not Gaussian.

stages.name: Minutes scenario given game script
stages.description: Conditional on a normal game, minutes depend on the projected margin: blowout favorites cut starters' fourth quarters, close games push stars past 38 minutes, overtime adds about five. Foul trouble forces bench stretches in the first half. DD probability is steeply increasing in minutes between roughly 26 and 36 and then flattens, so the distribution of minutes (not its mean) sets the probability.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed with a heavy left tail for blowouts and a point mass bump at 40+ for OT/close games; minutes and absolute margin are strongly (negatively) dependent.

stages.name: Lineup-conditional opportunity shares
stages.description: Each category's opportunity count is a share of a team-level pool: rebound chances come from missed shots by both teams times the player's board share, which is lower when another big is on the floor; assist chances come from teammate made shots on passes, which are lower when the primary creator is on the floor beside him. Teammate absences therefore reallocate production unevenly across categories, which is what turns a 20% DD player into a 45% one when the co-big sits.
stages.distribution: Multinomial-style allocation: shares are bounded and negatively dependent among teammates; pool size (pace x misses) is overdispersed.

stages.name: Category counts and their dependence
stages.description: Within minutes bucket, points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks are discrete, overdispersed counts. They co-move positively through shared minutes and pace but trade off within player: a high-usage scorer's assists fall as shots rise. A DD needs two of them to clear ten, so the dependence structure (how often pts and reb are both high) matters as much as the marginals, and the category pair differs by player archetype.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed negative-binomial-like marginals with role-dependent correlation of roughly +0.2 to +0.35 between reb and pts for bigs and slightly negative between pts and ast for guards; discrete threshold at 10.

stages.name: Threshold crossing, stat credit and settlement
stages.description: The final count is the official box score. A player at 9 with a few possessions left is a discrete lottery; late-game teammate gifting, intentional fouling and OT affect this tail. Assist and block credit are assigned by scorers with arena-specific habits, and post-game corrections can move a count across the line. The contract voids only inactive players, so no void protects an early-exit case.
stages.distribution: Binary indicator on integer counts; probability mass concentrated at 8-10 counts so single-event credit decisions flip outcomes.

talent_strength.note: Player-level DD base rate and path-specific rates by minutes bucket carry the talent signal; team strength enters only through game script.

opponent_matchup.note: Positional allowance is weak; opposing frontcourt size and assist-suppressing schemes act mainly through the lineup-conditional shares.

role_personnel.note: Who shares the floor determines board and assist shares; this is the most important category for DD.

availability_news.note: Own and teammate status, plus the in-game exit hazard that the voiding rule does not refund.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach-specific rotation length and stat-chase tolerance in decided games.

environment.note: Altitude, arena and travel effects on a single player's DD probability are second-order and are only reachable through minutes and pace; no separate venue variable is justified for this contract.

game_context_script.note: Blowout and close-game minutes truncation and OT extension of the count window.

pace_volume.note: Possession count scales rebound pool and assist chances.

efficiency_conversion.note: Assist conversion depends on teammate shot-making (potential assists strip it); scoring efficiency matters little for reaching ten points.

distribution_variance.note: Joint overdispersed counts and tail co-occurrence are the core of the model.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Back-to-back and clinch/rest effects on minutes for individual stars are not represented by any input of this archetype and are folded into projected minutes without an explicit variable.

officiating_rules.note: Scorer credit for assists, rebounds and blocks and post-game corrections matter at the 9/10 boundary.

settlement_contract.note: Five-category definition, voiding rule and postponement window are in the sampled rules.

nba.dd_category_pair_mix.label: Category-pair decomposition of a player's double-double paths (pts/reb/ast/stl/blk)
nba.dd_category_pair_mix.mechanism: A DD is a union over category pairs; each pair has its own minutes-sensitivity, so the player's probability is a mixture of path-specific probabilities.
nba.dd_category_pair_mix.rationale: A center reaches DD mainly via points+rebounds, a point-forward via points+assists, a rim-protecting big via reb+blk; one scalar 'DD rate' averages over paths whose responses to minutes, blowouts and absences differ, and omits the blocks/steals paths that the contract explicitly counts.
nba.dd_category_pair_mix.measurement: For each player-game with >=12 minutes over current + prior 2 seasons, flag each of 5 categories >=10; compute per-category P(>=10 | minutes bucket 12-20/20-28/28-34/34+) with exponential half-life of 45 games and beta shrinkage toward the position-archetype mean with prior weight 20 games; build pair-path rates P(pair) via joint empirical counts (not products). Output per player: vector of pair-path rates and the share of historical DDs coming from each pair. As-of: only games finished before the tip-off timestamp.
raw_data: boxscore traditional: player,game,min,pts,reb,ast,stl,blk
position/role archetype table
nba.dd_category_pair_mix.why: Lets the DD forecast respond correctly when a missing teammate changes which category pair is available (e.g. a guard's reb+ast path versus a big's pts+reb path).

nba.midgame_exit_hazard.label: In-game early-exit hazard (injury, ejection, foul-out, minutes cap)
nba.midgame_exit_hazard.mechanism: Once a player enters the game the contract settles on his stats even if he plays 5 minutes, so truncation by an early exit converts directly into NO.
nba.midgame_exit_hazard.rationale: The rules void only players who are inactive or never take the court; an injury exit after 6 minutes settles NO at near-certainty. The hazard is player-specific (age, injury history, listed status, foul rate) and is distinct from planned blowout minutes cuts.
nba.midgame_exit_hazard.measurement: From play-by-play, per player-season count games with >=1 minute where minutes < 0.55 x pregame-expected minutes and the exit was not a blowout rest (margin<15 at exit) divided by games entered; classify cause by sub-in/sub-out and injury report. Combine as hazard per 36 minutes with beta(2,40) prior shrinkage and a status multiplier (probable/questionable-return/minutes-restricted) estimated from historical status vintages. As-of: injury report at the latest vintage before tip.
raw_data: PBP substitutions/ejections
injury report vintages
box score minutes
nba.midgame_exit_hazard.why: DD is a threshold on cumulative production, so lost minutes from an in-game exit are not refunded; this tail is invisible in season-average minutes.

nba.late_threshold_assist_rebound_giftin.label: Late-game stat-chase and teammate-gifting effect near the 10 threshold
nba.late_threshold_assist_rebound_giftin.mechanism: When a player sits at 9 rebounds or assists in a decided game, teammates and coaches have been observed to funnel the last opportunity, so production near the threshold is not a smooth Poisson continuation.
nba.late_threshold_assist_rebound_giftin.rationale: Garbage-time minutes are normally a pure loss for DD, but stat-chasing partially offsets it; the size is team and coach specific and can be estimated from play-by-play without any market data. It is subtle because it only applies at 8-9 counts with margin >12 late.
nba.late_threshold_assist_rebound_giftin.measurement: From play-by-play, take all instances where a player enters the final 8 game minutes with margin >=12 and a category count of 8 or 9; compute observed rate of reaching 10 per remaining on-court minute divided by that player's baseline per-minute rate in the same category; pool by coach with empirical-Bayes shrinkage (prior weight 25 instances) and report the multiplier. Use as a pregame-fixed multiplier applied only inside the blowout branch.
raw_data: PBP event stream with score margin and player counts
coach tenure table
nba.late_threshold_assist_rebound_giftin.why: Corrects the mechanical over-penalty of blowout branches for near-threshold players; sign is opposite to the naive minutes-cut story.

nba.dd_center_swap_share.label: Rebound/assist share conditional on which co-big or creator shares the floor
nba.dd_center_swap_share.mechanism: Boards and assist chances are split among on-court teammates, so a player's DD path depends on which specific teammates occupy the other four slots in each rotation segment.
nba.dd_center_swap_share.rationale: Season rebound or assist percentage averages over very different lineups; the relevant quantity is the player's share when paired with tonight's expected 5-man units, weighted by expected minutes in each unit.
nba.dd_center_swap_share.measurement: From stint-level data compute the player's TRB% and AST% per lineup context (with each frequent teammate on/off, min 150 possessions) using ridge-regularised on/off coefficients (lambda tuned by rolling CV on prior season); then project tonight's expected minute-weighted lineup mix from rotation history and injury report and sum. Report a minutes-weighted expected board share and assist share with their standard errors.
raw_data: lineup-level possessions, TRB, AST, on/off
projected rotation
nba.dd_center_swap_share.why: A DD for a center is gated by whether the second big plays beside or behind him; the existing frontcourt competition input is not attached to this archetype.

nba.milestone_rates.reason: Right object (per-player P(>=10 in a category) by minutes bucket) but as written it is only the marginal base rate; it ignores blocks and steals as the second/third category for bigs and wings, so it must be rebuilt per category pair rather than as one DD flag.

nba.minutes.reason: Minutes is the common multiplier of all three counting components and the DD indicator is steeply threshold-like in it; useful only if delivered as a scenario mixture (starter-normal, blowout-cut, foul-trouble, early exit, OT) not a single point projection.

nba.stat_dist.reason: Per-stat marginals are needed but a product of marginals is exactly the wrong DD model; this input is subordinate to the joint model, and its overdispersion parameters should be conditional on minutes bucket.

nba.combo_covariance.reason: Dependence is the heart of a conjunction, but a single covariance number is a poor summary of tail co-occurrence; needs conditional-on-minutes dependence or a copula, and sign differs by role (pts/ast trade off for guards, pts/reb co-move through pace and minutes for bigs).

nba.reb_chances.reason: Rebound chances are the stable driver behind the rebound component for centers and forwards; it is secondary here only because it cannot by itself produce a DD without a second category.

nba.pot_ast.reason: Potential assists (passes leading to shots) strips teammate shot-making luck out of the assist component, which is the right variable for guards and point-forwards who reach 10 assists.

nba.usage.reason: Usage explains the points component only; for the dominant DD path of a rebounding big (pts+reb) it adds little beyond minutes, and for assist-first guards it moves inversely with the ast component, so as a lone scalar it is mislabelled secondary signal.

nba.garbage.reason: Blowout minute loss is the dominant reason favorites' stars miss DD; but the label says 'from spread' which is a market-derived quantity, so the input must be rebuilt from team ratings and rotation history, with the spread only as a benchmark.

nba.teammate_absence_shift.reason: A missing co-big or primary creator reallocates boards or assists to a specific player and can move DD probability by 15-25 points; with/without splits are small-sample, so shrinkage toward a role-based allocation prior is required.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Own and teammate status vintages are the main source of mispricing around a binary event; inactive players are voided at a fair price so only the active-but-limited branch matters for the settled outcome.

m.quote_history.reason: A price path is a market observable, not a causal driver of double-double production; useful only to date when news was absorbed relative to the injury-report vintage.

m.rules_text.reason: Settlement wording genuinely changes the event (five categories counted, inactive or never-entered players refunded at a fair price, 48h postponement window) and must be versioned per series.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook DD/TD prices are a benchmark to compare a fundamentals model against, not an input; including them would hide the model's own information content.

nba.stat_corrections.reason: Official stat corrections (assist or rebound credit changed after review) can flip a player sitting exactly at 9 vs 10 in a category; rare but relevant to settlement timing, context-only.

nba.opp_def_pos.reason: Opponent-allowed-by-position tables are noisy, confounded with pace and opponent shot mix, and DD events are far too rare for the positional allowance signal to be estimated per matchup; use only as a heavily shrunk adjustment.

nba.pace.reason: Pace scales all three components but the DD effect is second-order relative to minutes; useful through the rebound pool rather than as a standalone variable.

interactions.mechanism: DD probability is nearly flat above ~34 minutes and falls steeply below ~26, so a blowout that trims a starter from 35 to 28 minutes costs far more than one trimming 38 to 33; the effect is largest for players whose second category is marginal (rebounds around 8).
interactions.how_to_test: Fit P(DD) against projected minutes in 3-minute bins separately for blowout-probability terciles; look for a kink near 28-30 minutes that differs by tercile.

interactions.mechanism: A center's rebound chances are shared with the other big only when both are on the floor, so the same rebound pool yields different counts depending on the fraction of minutes spent paired versus alone; direction is positive for the survivor when the co-big is out.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare a center's DD rate in games with vs without each frequent co-big (matched on minutes, opponent pace) and test against the lineup-weighted share prediction.

interactions.mechanism: A fast game raises misses, possessions and assist chances together, which fattens the joint upper tail of rebounds and points more than the marginals alone; this correlates the two required components of a pts+reb DD and increases conjunction probability beyond the product of marginals.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(pts>=10 and reb>=10) versus the product of marginals by opponent-pair pace tercile; the excess ratio should rise with pace.

interactions.mechanism: A designated player is in one of two regimes: normal-load or limited/returning; in the latter the exit hazard and minute cap shift probability mass to very short appearances which settle NO, and the voiding rule does not help.
interactions.how_to_test: Split historical entries by pregame status vintage and compare the fraction of games with <55% of expected minutes and the resulting DD rate.

interactions.mechanism: Inside the blowout branch, a player at 9 in a category late is more likely than his per-minute rate implies to finish, because teammates funnel the last opportunity; this partially offsets the minutes loss, in the direction opposite to the naive blowout penalty.
interactions.how_to_test: Among decided games, regress P(reach 10) from count 8-9 entering the last 8 minutes on baseline per-minute rate and a stat-chase coach indicator.

nonlinearities.shape: S-shaped/saturating: steep between ~24 and ~34 projected minutes then flat
nonlinearities.why: The count window for every category scales with minutes but the ten-count threshold turns a linear mean into a sigmoid probability; extra minutes beyond 36 add little for a player who already clears 10 in one category.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in per-minute category rate near the threshold
nonlinearities.why: A per-minute rebound rate that implies a mean of 8.5 versus 10.5 in 34 minutes changes P(>=10) from ~35% to ~60%; conjunction of two such events makes the DD probability convex in each category mean.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold: little effect below ~15% blowout probability, steep above ~35%
nonlinearities.why: Starters' minutes are cut only when the margin crosses ~15-20 with a few minutes left, so blowout probability matters mostly in the tail; the effect is non-linear in the team-rating gap.

contract.settlement_definition: Archetype holds many series: the standard ladders (points N+ with floor_strike at N-0.5) settle YES if the named player's official points (and for PRA combined points+rebounds+assists) reach the strike in the named game; inactive or never-entering players settle at a fair price, and once he enters the market settles on actual stats; games postponed but played within 48 hours stay open, otherwise fair price. KXNBAH2HPRA compares two players (YES if the named player has more combined PRA, 50/50 on equal totals, fair price if either does not enter or if the game is cancelled/postponed beyond two weeks). KXNBAESCALATORPTS is scalar: payout floor(10000 x (y/50)^3)/10000 where y is points rounded down to even and capped at 50. Most other series in the archetype are TITLE_ONLY.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player enters the game the market settles based on the player's combined points, rebounds, and assists recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Confirms combined-stat ladder settles on actual PRA once the player enters; no refund for early exit.

rules_evidence.quote: If both players enter the game and record an equal number of combined points, rebounds, and assists, then all markets resolve to 50/50.
rules_evidence.establishes: Head-to-head ties are settled 50/50 rather than NO, so a tie is half-credit and discreteness of the difference matters.

rules_evidence.quote: or the game is cancelled or postponed more than two weeks, then all markets resolve to a fair market price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Variant: the H2H postponement window is two weeks, versus 48 hours on the single-player ladders.

rules_evidence.quote: y = min(50, max(0, 2 x floor(s / 2)))
rules_evidence.establishes: Scalar payout depends on points rounded down to an even number and capped at 50; payout is cubic in y, so tail points dominate expected value.

variants_and_edge_cases: Scalar escalator (KXNBAESCALATORPTS): payout floor(10000 x (y / 50)^3) / 10000 with y = min(50, max(0, 2 x floor(s / 2))); value is E[(y/50)^3], so the quantity needed is the whole points distribution, in particular the tail above 30, not a threshold probability.

Head-to-head (KXNBAH2HPRA): resolves on the difference of two players' combined counts; ties pay 50/50 and neither-enters or beyond-two-week postponement gives a fair price; requires joint distribution of two players.

Protected (KXNBAPTSPROT) and leader/race series (KXNBAPTSLEADER, KXNBARACE, KXNBAFIRST50PTS), season-long (KXNBAPTSALLGAMES) and the all-star 3-point contest (KXNBA3PTCONTEST) are filed here but are TITLE_ONLY and follow different mechanics; their rules are not verified.
Standard ladders void inactive or never-entering players at a fair price but not players who exit early, so a first-quarter injury settles NO.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box score points / combined statistics as named in the full Kalshi rules; sampled secondary text for PRA is truncated before naming the source agencies, so the exact sources are unverified.

mechanism.summary: Points are minutes times a possession-and-usage-driven attempt rate times conversion, with free throws added. The causal chain is: availability and minutes scenario (a mixture, not a mean), team possessions available while he is on court (matchup pace and game script), his share of those possessions given the specific five-man unit on the floor, shot mix and shot quality against this defense, free-throw trips from foul drawing and the opponent's foul rate, game-script truncation or extension (blowout rest, late intentional fouling, overtime), and finally the settlement form, which differs across the series in this archetype (threshold ladders, combined-stat ladders, head-to-head with 50/50 ties, a cubic scalar payout). Each stage adds variance of a different shape: discrete mixture for minutes, overdispersed count for attempts, Bernoulli noise with heavy shrinkage for makes, so the upper rungs are governed by scenario weights and tails rather than by the mean.

stages.name: Availability and minutes scenario mixture
stages.description: The scorer either enters the game or is voided; conditional on entering he plays under one of several scenarios: a normal starter workload of 32-36 minutes, a blowout trim to 26-30, foul-trouble stretches, a minutes restriction, an early exit, or overtime adding about five. The 30+ and 40+ rungs are reachable only in the full-load branch, so scenario weights set rung probabilities more than the player's mean points do. Status vintages and the calibrated probability that a questionable player plays feed this stage.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture with a long left tail and an OT bump; weights depend jointly on status, margin and fouls; not unimodal.

stages.name: Possessions available on court
stages.description: The number of possessions in the game is a joint product of both teams' pace, not either team's average, and a scorer's share of the possessions he is on court for is minutes divided by 48 weighted by stint timing. Pace shifts with lineup (a slow big lineup vs a small-ball unit) and with game state (trailing teams speed up late). Possessions scale attempts nearly proportionally, but the market total is a price and cannot stand in for it.
stages.distribution: Roughly Gaussian game possessions (sd about 6-7) but with lineup-dependent mean shifts and right skew from OT; fed into a Poisson-like attempt process.

stages.name: Usage allocation within the on-court unit
stages.description: Given possessions, the team's shot, free-throw trip and turnover events are divided among the five on court. A scorer's share rises when specific teammates are absent (a ball-dominant guard out raises a wing's share more than a rim-runner's), and falls when another creator enters. This is estimated better by a unit-level allocation model with creation archetypes than by per-teammate with/without splits.
stages.distribution: Dirichlet/multinomial shares; negatively correlated across teammates; attempts per game overdispersed relative to Poisson, variance rising with usage.

stages.name: Shot quality and conversion
stages.description: Points per attempt depend on the shooter's mix of rim, midrange and three attempts, defender proximity, and the opponent's scheme (drop gives pull-up midrange and threes, switch gives post mismatches, blitz gives short-roll chances). Single-game make rates are noise around talent, and shrinkage constants differ by shot type, so recent hot streaks should be heavily discounted except for rim finishing and free throws.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli sums with heterogeneous probability; variance dominated by binomial noise (for 18 attempts, sd of points about 5); heavy shrinkage required.

stages.name: Free-throw trips and officiating
stages.description: Free throws add points at 75-90% conversion depending on the shooter; trips are generated by drives and post touches and by opponent fouling, with crew-level foul-call tendency and the team-foul bonus state adding variance. Late-game intentional fouls add attempts for ball handlers. A scorer with a high free throw rate has a less volatile points distribution than a three-point-dependent one.
stages.distribution: Count of trips overdispersed; conversion binomial per trip with high-probability tail; a few late-game extras skew guards' right tail.

stages.name: Distribution, dependence and settlement form
stages.description: The ladder rung is a threshold probability from one distribution; the escalator is the expectation of a cubic payoff; the head-to-head contract requires the joint law of two players with ties at 50/50; combined-stat ladders need dependence between components. The same minutes-and-usage structure feeds all, but tail shape and cross-player dependence differ, so the contract form determines which distributional features must be accurate.
stages.distribution: Integer-valued, right-skewed, heavy upper tail; joint with correlated components; payoff convex (cubic) for the scalar form.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent scheme and shot allowance matched to the scorer's own shot-type mix.

coaching_scheme.note: Rotation length and defensive coverage choices of both coaches.

environment.note: Altitude and travel effects exist but are small relative to rotation and usage changes; handled as context.

efficiency_conversion.note: Per-shot expected points with shrinkage and FT conversion.

distribution_variance.note: Minutes-conditional overdispersion, heavy tail for the cubic scalar and cross-player dependence for H2H/combined products.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest-day and playoff-seeding stakes affect star minutes but only back-to-back/travel is represented; clinch-and-rest incentives and minutes-restriction ramp-ups after injury have no explicit input.

officiating_rules.note: Crew foul tendency and team bonus state shift free-throw trips.

settlement_contract.note: Per-series settlement forms differ (ladder, H2H 50/50 tie, scalar cubic payout, protected variants) and must be tracked.

nba.pts_exit_foulout_hazard.label: Early-exit and foul-out hazard of the scorer (injury, ejection, sixth foul)
nba.pts_exit_foulout_hazard.mechanism: Points accumulate only while on court and the contract settles on actual points once he enters, so mid-game exits remove the upper tail entirely.
nba.pts_exit_foulout_hazard.rationale: Average minutes hide a distribution with a point mass at early departure; for older or injury-prone scorers and foul-prone drivers it is several percent per game and it is not captured by status labels alone.
nba.pts_exit_foulout_hazard.measurement: From box score and play-by-play, per player-season: share of games entered with minutes < 0.55 x pregame expected minutes and a non-blowout exit, plus share ending by sixth foul or ejection; beta(2,40) shrinkage to a position prior, 60-game half-life; multiply by a status factor for Questionable/Probable/returning-from-injury estimated from archived report vintages. Feeds a mixture weight for the short-minutes branch.
raw_data: PBP sub/ejection/foul events
injury vintages
minutes
nba.pts_exit_foulout_hazard.why: Upper rungs (25+, 30+) require a full-load game; a few percent mass on short appearances moves their probabilities by absolute 1-3 points and is not in any existing input.

nba.usage_allocation_model.label: Lineup-conditional shot-attempt allocation model for tonight's expected on-court unit
nba.usage_allocation_model.mechanism: Team attempts are a roughly fixed pie divided among the five on court according to creation roles, so a scorer's share is a function of the whole unit, not just whether one named teammate is out.
nba.usage_allocation_model.rationale: With/without splits rest on tiny samples and ignore that replacing a creator by a catch-and-shoot wing shifts shots differently than replacing him by another creator; an allocation model with role types generalises across rosters.
nba.usage_allocation_model.measurement: Fit a Dirichlet-multinomial (or softmax) model of FGA+0.44*FTA+TOV shares among the five on-court players using stint data, with player creation archetype, on-ball minutes share and prior-season usage as features; ridge-regularised, 2-season window with 200-game half-life; predict tonight's shares for the projected unit set (weighted by expected minutes per unit) and report mean and standard error. As-of: injury report at last vintage.
raw_data: lineup stints possessions, FGA, FTA, TOV by player
creation archetype table
nba.usage_allocation_model.why: Gives a generalisable replacement for noisy with/without splits and quantifies the usage a scorer inherits when a particular type of teammate is absent.

nba.cross_player_points_dependence.label: Dependence of points across players (teammates, opponents, same player multi-stat)
nba.cross_player_points_dependence.mechanism: Teammates compete for the same possessions (negative within team conditional on total) while all players share pace and shooting variance of the game (positive across teams), which sets joint-event probabilities.
nba.cross_player_points_dependence.rationale: Head-to-head, combined-stat and points-leader products are functions of the joint law of several players' points; marginals alone give wrong answers, e.g. two opponent stars' point difference has a variance depending on the sign of their correlation.
nba.cross_player_points_dependence.measurement: Estimate pairwise correlations of residual points (actual minus minutes-conditional expectation) for same-team and opposite-team pairs over a 2-season window with Fisher-z shrinkage toward position-pair prior (weight 40 games); also correlation of a player's points with his own rebounds+assists residuals for PRA/PR/PA products. Cross-team pairs typically near +0.1 via pace; same-team pairs typically negative.
raw_data: player-game residuals from the minutes-conditional model
nba.cross_player_points_dependence.why: Needed for KXNBAH2H*, PRA-type and leader contracts in this archetype where the event is a comparison or sum of several players' counts.

nba.points_upper_tail_rate.label: Player-specific upper-tail frequency of points given full-minutes games (ceiling-game rate)
nba.points_upper_tail_rate.mechanism: Scoring has a heavier right tail than a negative binomial fit to the mean implies because hot shooting, FT surges and OT stack; the cubic escalator weights this tail heavily.
nba.points_upper_tail_rate.rationale: The scalar escalator pays (y/50)^3 so its expected value is dominated by 35+ outcomes; a model calibrated to the mean misprices it, and the 30+/40+ rungs depend on the same tail.
nba.points_upper_tail_rate.measurement: For each player estimate exceedance probabilities P(pts >= 1.4m), P(pts >= 1.7m) and P(pts>=2.0m) where m is the minutes-conditional mean, on games with >=30 minutes over a 3-season window; fit a generalised-Pareto above the 85th percentile of residuals with shape shrunk to a league-wide value (prior weight 60 exceedances). Output the tail index and exceedance rates.
raw_data: player-game points and expected points
nba.points_upper_tail_rate.why: Directly prices KXNBAESCALATORPTS and the 30+/40+ rungs, where tail shape, not the mean, drives value.

nba.player_xpts_per_shot.label: Shot-level expected points per attempt for the player vs tonight's defense
nba.player_xpts_per_shot.mechanism: Points per attempt is a function of shot type (rim, midrange, catch-and-shoot three), defender proximity and the shooter's finishing talent, so team zone averages mix very different shooters.
nba.player_xpts_per_shot.rationale: Opponent zone-allowed tables ignore who takes the shots; a pull-up scorer vs drop coverage and a roll man vs switching differ by large amounts and these are mostly knowable pregame.
nba.player_xpts_per_shot.measurement: From shot-level data estimate a hierarchical model of make probability by player x shot type x defender-distance bin with beta priors (rim prior weight 150 FGA, three prior weight 750 FGA, midrange 300); multiply by opponent's allowed frequency/quality for each shot type (opponent-adjusted by league mean) to get predicted points per shot; sum over projected attempts by type. As-of: shots finished before tip-off.
free_sources: nba_api shotchartdetail and tracking shot dashboards
raw_data: shot chart: loc_x, loc_y, shot_type, result
closest-defender-distance tracking (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for public completeness)
nba.player_xpts_per_shot.why: Separates shot-making skill from volume for 20+ rungs and makes opponent scheme matter only where the scorer's shot types intersect it.

nba.minutes.reason: Largest variance source for a points ladder; must enter as a scenario mixture (normal, blowout cut, foul trouble, early exit, OT) because the 30+ and 40+ rungs are only reachable in the high-minutes branch.

nba.usage.reason: Shot and free-throw-trip share is what converts minutes to points; but season usage is an average over lineups, so it must be conditioned on who is on the floor tonight (see usage allocation).

nba.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Redistribution when a co-star sits is the main non-market information on scoring ladders; weakness is tiny with/without samples, so it needs shrinkage to a role-based allocation model.

nba.implied_team_totals.reason: Derived from the sportsbook spread and total, so it is a market price repackaged as a variable; it should be a benchmark for a ratings-built team total, not a model input.

nba.garbage.reason: Blowout-driven minute loss shrinks upper-rung probability disproportionately; needs rebuilding from ratings and rotation history instead of the spread, which is a market observable.

nba.shot_profile.reason: Team-level zone mix allowed is a reasonable shot-quality prior but is too coarse for player points; it must be matched to the shooter's own zone distribution.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Drop vs switch vs blitz changes which scorers get clean pull-up or roll looks; categorical scheme labels are noisy and should be interacted with the scorer's play-type mix, not used as main effects.

nba.matchup_def.reason: Primary-defender assignment is unknown pregame and shifts within the game via switching; effect sizes for a single defender are small and statistically indistinguishable from noise at single-game scale.

nba.ft_attempts.reason: Foul drawing is a stable skill and converts to efficient points; opponent foul rate allowed is the second half of the definition and is the part that varies game to game.

nba.referee_crew.reason: Crew foul-call tendency shifts team FTA modestly and is only known at roughly 9am on game day; small once opponent foul rate is included.

nba.player_shooting_regression.reason: Prevents overweighting a hot 10-game stretch; but it is a single bundle for 3P%, FG% and FT% whose shrinkage speeds are very different (FT% is stable, 3P% needs ~750 attempts), so it should be split by component.

nba.pace.reason: Possessions scale attempts, but matchup pace is not the mean of two team paces; the lineup-aware version is needed and the market total should not stand in for it.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Second night of a back-to-back lowers minutes and efficiency slightly; effect is small relative to rotation changes and mostly acts through projected minutes.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Own and co-star status vintage drives both minutes and usage reallocation; point-in-time discipline is the entire value.

nba.status_resolution_prob.reason: Calibrated play probability matters for questionable players but the contract refunds inactive players, so it matters only through the limited-minutes branch of those who do play.

nba.stat_dist.reason: Overdispersion and discreteness of points shape the upper rungs and the escalator payout; must be minutes-conditional rather than one distribution per player.

m.quote_history.reason: Price path is a market observable useful for timing news absorption, not a determinant of points scored.

m.rules_text.reason: Rules differ materially inside this archetype: 48h postponement vs two-week window in H2H, tie resolving 50/50, scalar escalator payouts, protected contracts.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook points lines are a benchmark prior; feeding them as an input leaves the model with no independent information.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung monotonicity is a diagnostic of quote quality, not of points production; a model's own ladder should be monotone by construction.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Execution realism only; says nothing about the data-generating process.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Realized frequency per rung is label history for calibration, not a causal input.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: Price-bucket bias of the Kalshi book; this is a calibration overlay on model output, not an input to the scoring process.

m.volume_oi.reason: Liquidity rank has no mechanism link to points; weak even as a discount factor because volume is itself driven by player popularity.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trades are market microstructure; informed-flow hypotheses are untested and belong in an overlay, not the points model.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Settled values are labels; needed to reconcile with the official box score used for resolution.

nba.stat_corrections.reason: Official points are rarely revised (assist/rebound credit changes far more often), so this is a low-value item for points ladders.

nba.player_role_position.reason: Maps opponent-by-role data to the scorer, but five-position labels are too crude; creation type (on-ball, off-ball, roll) is the usable version.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Intentional fouling in close games adds free throws for ball handlers; real but concentrated in the last two minutes of games decided by under 8 points.

interactions.mechanism: When a co-star is out the scorer's usage rises but true shooting typically falls (harder shots, fewer assisted looks), so points rise by far less than usage; the loss is largest when the absent player is a primary creator whose assists generated the scorer's easy shots.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress points-per-possession on usage change interacted with absent-creator indicator using stint data; check that the slope on usage is below 1 only for assisted-shot-heavy scorers.

interactions.mechanism: Blowout probability trims minutes only in the fourth-quarter tail, which removes the high-minutes branch where 30+ outcomes live; the 30+ rung is therefore several times more sensitive to blowout probability than the 15+ rung.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot realised hit rate of 15+, 25+ and 35+ against pregame blowout-probability tercile; the log-odds slope should grow with the rung.

interactions.mechanism: A drop-coverage defense raises expected points for a pull-up midrange scorer and lowers it for a roll finisher with the same usage; a switching defense does the opposite via mismatch creation, so scheme effects are conditional on shot type, not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact opponent scheme label with scorer play-type share in a shot-level make model; test cross-term significance out of sample.

interactions.mechanism: In H2H and combined contracts the variance of the difference between two opponents' points depends on whether the pair is positively correlated through pace; a fast game raises both counts, so tail differences shrink while teammates' contests inherit a negative correlation.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute realised variance of (A-B) points vs predicted from marginals only, split by pace tercile and by same-team vs opposite-team pairs.

interactions.mechanism: A player flagged questionable or just back from injury lives in a different minutes regime where the early-exit hazard rises several fold; the standard ladders refund only inactive players, so exits in the active state settle NO.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the fraction of early-exit games across status vintages and check the calibration of the mixture weights against realised short-minute rates.

nonlinearities.shape: concave: points per possession falls as usage rises
nonlinearities.why: Marginal shots taken by a scorer inheriting a teammate's usage are lower-quality (more contested, fewer assisted), so the points response to usage is below proportional and flattens above roughly 30% usage.

nonlinearities.shape: convex payout weight: cubic escalator and heavy right tail
nonlinearities.why: Escalator payout is (y/50)^3, so a 40-point game pays ~51% while a 25-point game pays ~11%; expected payout is dominated by the upper tail and by the generalised-Pareto shape, so small tail-index errors create large payout errors.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise: near-linear 20-34 minutes, then flattening, with a bump from OT
nonlinearities.why: Per-minute scoring is roughly constant for starters, but rungs above 30 points need >34 minutes in most cases; OT creates a step increase that matters for the tail.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold at margin about 18-20 with 6-8 minutes left
nonlinearities.why: Starters are pulled only after a decisive margin, so the minutes effect is small until blowout probability exceeds roughly one-third and then steep.

contract.settlement_definition: Binary ladder on one player's official rebounds in the named game: YES if rebounds are at or above N (floor_strike N-0.5, strike_type greater, titles like '10+ rebounds'). Inactive or never-entering players settle at a fair price; once he enters the market settles on actual rebounds. A postponed game that begins within 48 hours stays open, otherwise all markets resolve at a fair price. The protected variant (KXNBAREBPROT) additionally refunds, at the pre-tip fair price, a player who enters in the first half but not after halftime (including overtime), unless he already has the required rebounds. Series leader markets in the ledger are TITLE_ONLY.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player enters the game the market settles based on the player's rebounds recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Standard rebound ladder settles on actual rebounds once the player enters; no early-exit protection.

rules_evidence.quote: this Contract resolves to the fair price prior to the opening tip of the game unless the player records the required number of rebounds
rules_evidence.establishes: Protected variant: first-half-only participation is refunded at the pre-tip fair price unless the threshold was already met.

rules_evidence.quote: If the player enters the game after the conclusion of the first half, this Contract settles based on actual statistics, regardless of first-half participation.
rules_evidence.establishes: Protection switches off once the player appears after halftime, so the voided branch is exactly first-half-only appearances.

variants_and_edge_cases: Protected (KXNBAREBPROT) vs standard (KXNBAREB) on the same player and strike have different payoffs for the same early-exit event; a model must carry both forms.
Sampled strikes include 10+ for a wing (Mario Hezonja, floor_strike 9.5) which is a far-tail rung; ladder rungs span the tail and low-probability rungs are dominated by pool variance not talent.
Overtime is not addressed in the sampled standard text; official box score rebounds normally include OT, adding five minutes of pool in about 6% of games.
Series rebounds leader (KXNBASERIESREBLEADER) is a multi-game argmax with TITLE_ONLY rules; mechanism and tie handling unverified.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box-score rebounds as named in the full rules (the sampled secondary text is cut before listing source agencies, so the exact source and correction policy are unverified).

mechanism.summary: Rebounds are minutes times the rate at which missed shots (both teams') land within reach times the share of those the player secures. The chain is: participation and minutes (bigs are foul- and blowout-sensitive), the supply of creditable misses given pace, both teams' shot quality and the free-throw and team-rebound leakage, how that supply splits between offensive and defensive boards given each coach's crash policy, the player's share given which other rebounders are on the floor and where he stands (rim vs perimeter), conversion of chances to rebounds (contested vs uncontested, deferrals), and the distributional consequences: counts are overdispersed because the supply itself varies with shooting luck of both teams, and the shared supply makes teammates' rebound counts negatively dependent. The existing catalog captures supply and share conceptually but not the credit leakage, the lineup-pairing arithmetic or the protected-contract state.

stages.name: Appearance, minutes and foul exposure
stages.description: A big either plays a standard 28-36 minutes or loses time to foul trouble, a blowout, or an injury. Rebounds are strongly minutes-dependent, and bigs pick up early fouls that trigger first-half benching, so the minutes distribution has a heavy left tail. For protected contracts the first-half-only branch has a distinct payoff.
stages.distribution: Minutes mixture with a left-tail mass from fouls and blowouts; foul accumulation is a count process with a coach-specific benching threshold (two early, three in first half).

stages.name: Supply of creditable misses
stages.description: The number of missed shots is the sum of two teams' misses, a function of pace and each side's shot quality; part of the supply is lost to team rebounds, out-of-bounds recoveries and dead free-throw attempts. High-scoring, high-FG% games shrink the pool, while games with bad shooting enlarge it, which makes rebounds negatively correlated with total points.
stages.distribution: Supply approximately normal with sd of about 5-6 misses but with a negative dependence on shooting luck; leakage varies with foul volume.

stages.name: Offensive and defensive split by team strategy
stages.description: Offensive rebounds depend on how many players crash and how the opponent defends the glass; defensive boards depend on the opponent's attack style and whether players leak out in transition. A big on a crashing team has a higher offensive component with more variance. Opponent scheme (drop vs switching) positions centers near or far from the rim.
stages.distribution: OREB count is a thinned process with team-specific rate; DREB dominates the mean but OREB adds right-tail variance.

stages.name: Share among on-court rebounders
stages.description: Given a creditable miss, who secures it depends on position, box-out assignment and the other bigs on the floor. The share is lineup-specific: a center's TRB% is far higher beside four perimeter players than beside another big. Teammate absences reallocate shares to specific survivors, and bench bigs inherit starters' shares only partly.
stages.distribution: Shares are bounded, sum to one across the five on court (negative dependence among teammates); share estimates carry sampling error that depends on possessions together.

stages.name: Count distribution and settlement
stages.description: Conditional on supply and share, the count is overdispersed relative to Poisson and discrete at the strike; rungs near the mean are very sensitive to dispersion. Scorer credit for team rebounds and rare video-review corrections matter only at exact-threshold counts. Settlement uses the official box score with a fair-price refund only for inactive players (or first-half-only in the protected series).
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial-like with dispersion driven by pool variance and minutes mixture; integer counts; rung probabilities concentrated in a 7-12 range.

nba.creditable_rebound_pool.label: Player-creditable rebound pool: misses net of team rebounds and dead-ball leakage
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.mechanism: Official player rebounds exclude team rebounds (shot-clock violations, balls out of bounds, first free-throw misses of a pair), so the pool a player can be credited from is smaller than total misses and varies by game flow.
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.rationale: A pool built from field-goal misses alone overstates supply when games have many foul-heavy trips, where missed first free throws and dead-ball team rebounds produce no player rebound; the leakage is about 6-10% of misses and varies with foul rate.
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.measurement: For each team-game: creditable_pool = FG misses + live FT misses (last free throw of a trip) - (team rebounds + out-of-bounds recoveries); estimate team-level leakage ratio by regressing team rebounds on FG misses, FT trips and out-of-bounds counts over 2 seasons with 80-game half-life; project tonight's pool as projected combined misses (ratings and shot-quality based, not market totals) times (1 - projected leakage). Leakage uses opponent foul rate and arena (scorer) effect.
free_sources: nba_api team box scores (reb, oreb, dreb, team reb)
raw_data: team box scores incl. team rebound counts
PBP FT and out-of-bounds events
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.why: Fixes the denominator of the rebound process; bigs in foul-heavy games see a smaller player-creditable pool even when total misses are high.

nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.label: Rebound percentage conditional on specific frontcourt pairings (ridge on/off)
nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.mechanism: A big's share of available boards depends on which other rebounders share the floor in each stint; the same player has very different shares beside a stretch four vs a second center.
nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.rationale: Season TRB% averages over pairings; because rotation patterns change with injury news, what matters is the expected minute-weighted mix of tonight's pairings, which is predictable pregame once availability is known.
nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.measurement: From stint data, regress player TRB% on indicator vectors of teammates on court (ridge, lambda chosen by rolling-origin CV on previous season, minimum 150 possessions per pair) with opponent offensive-rebounding strength as a covariate; project tonight's stint mix = rotation minutes by lineup weighted by injury-conditioned availability; output expected share and its standard error. DREB% and OREB% estimated separately because OREB is lineup-sensitive.
raw_data: lineup stints: possessions, player oreb/dreb, opp misses while on court
nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.why: Turns the unquantified frontcourt competition label into a number and links it to injury-conditioned rotation changes.

nba.team_glass_strategy.label: Offensive-glass crash rate versus transition-defense tradeoff of each team and coach
nba.team_glass_strategy.mechanism: Coaches choose how many players crash the offensive boards; heavy crashing raises OREB for bigs and lowers the opponent's DREB share while increasing transition possessions for opponents.
nba.team_glass_strategy.rationale: Crash policy is a team trait that is persistent across seasons within a coach, and it changes both rebound counts and pace; it is not recoverable from rebound pool or pace alone.
nba.team_glass_strategy.measurement: Compute per team-season OREB% and opponent transition points per possession after offensive rebounds (from play-by-play possession types) with 70-game half-life and coach-tenure reset; build matchup term = own crash rate x opponent weakness against crashing (opponent's DREB% minus expected from size) and report separately for OREB and DREB attributable to the player's position.
raw_data: possession start type, oreb counts, transition scoring
nba.team_glass_strategy.why: Adjusts the side-specific mix (OREB vs DREB) which the pooled rebound total hides; relevant for forwards who crash.

nba.big_exit_protection_state.label: Big-man early-exit and first-half-only participation hazard, mapped to protected-contract voiding
nba.big_exit_protection_state.mechanism: Bigs foul out and tweak ankles at higher rates, and protected rebound contracts refund players who play only the first half unless the threshold is already reached.
nba.big_exit_protection_state.rationale: In standard contracts an early exit settles NO; in protected series the same event refunds at a pre-tip fair price, so the same underlying hazard has opposite market consequences and must be tracked separately for the two forms.
nba.big_exit_protection_state.measurement: Per player-season, estimate P(minutes in 2H+OT = 0 | entered 1H) and P(exit before 12 total minutes) from play-by-play with beta(2,40) shrinkage and a status multiplier; output separately: hazard of 'plays only first half' (protected refund branch) and 'exits early without refund'. As-of: injury report vintage.
raw_data: PBP substitutions by half
injury vintages
nba.big_exit_protection_state.why: Needed to price KXNBAREBPROT correctly versus KXNBAREB for the same player and strike.

nba.minutes.reason: Rebound chances accrue per minute on court and bigs are the players most exposed to foul-driven benching; delivered as a mixture it also gives the fat left tail the existing text only mentions.

nba.reb_chances.reason: Chances (a rebound within reach) are far more stable than rebounds because conversion is largely deferred or contested; this is the correct first-stage variable but depends on tracking data that is only partly public.

nba.rebound_pool.reason: The supply of missed shots is the denominator of every rebound; as defined (expected misses by type) it omits the team-rebound leakage and free-throw-miss composition that determine how much of the supply a player can actually be credited with.

nba.frontcourt_competition.reason: Boards are zero-sum among the bigs on the floor, which makes this the key pairing variable; but only a label exists, no calculation, so it needs the pairing-adjusted board share defined below.

nba.teammate_absence_shift.reason: A missing big raises the survivor's share, but with/without samples for specific frontcourt pairs are small; shrink to role prior and combine with the pairing-adjusted share.

nba.shot_profile.reason: The opponent's three-point and rim attempt mix changes rebound distance and who gets the ball; useful but already partly present in the pool-by-type; second-order for centers.

nba.opp_def_pos.reason: Rebounds allowed to a position are dominated by pace, opponent miss volume and who was on the floor; as a positional average it largely repeats the pool and pairing inputs.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Drop coverage anchors the center near the rim (more boards), switching pulls him out and pushes rebounds to wings; effect real for the center, undetectable for guards.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Frontcourt availability of both teams (own co-big, opposing rebounders and rim protectors) sets shares; timing vintage matters.

nba.scorer_bias.reason: Arena-level credit differences are mainly for assists, steals and blocks; rebound credit is mostly objective except team-rebound assignment, so the effect is small compared with the Poisson noise at a 10+ threshold.

nba.stat_dist.reason: Overdispersion of rebounds is driven by the shared pool variance and minutes mixture; distribution must be conditional on both.

interactions.mechanism: Expected rebounds equal minutes share times the pool times conversion share, so a fast game of poor shooting multiplies the benefit of a full minutes load; in a blowout the pool is large but the starter is on the bench, leaving the product small.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress rebounds on log pool, log minutes and their product; check that the elasticity of minutes rises with pool size.

interactions.mechanism: The share a big inherits when another big is absent depends on which player replaces the minutes: a stretch forward replacing a rim-runner gives the survivor extra share, a second center gives little; so the absence effect is conditional on the replacement type, not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate absence effect separately by replacement archetype (big vs wing) with stint data and test equality of effects.

interactions.mechanism: A team that crashes the offensive glass concedes transition chances and plays slower after its own misses; opponent transition frequency changes pace and the miss supply in subsequent possessions, so crash policy has a nonlinear effect on the pool via pace.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare possession counts per 48 for high-crash vs low-crash teams, controlling for opponent, and relate to OREB totals.

interactions.mechanism: A big with a high foul rate in a lopsided game is likelier to be benched early in the first half and then not return, producing joint extreme left-tail minutes; the two sources of truncation are not independent because coaches avoid risking a foul-prone starter once the margin is large.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(minutes<20) by foul-rate tercile within blowout-probability terciles; test for a non-additive cell.

interactions.mechanism: A designated or returning big carries a first-half-only appearance hazard; protected contracts refund this branch while standard contracts settle NO, so identical status information has opposite value in the two series.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised first-half-only appearances by status vintage and test the resulting price gap between KXNBAREBPROT and KXNBAREB for the same strike.

nonlinearities.shape: concave: conversion share saturates as chances rise
nonlinearities.why: Chances above a player's available share increase contested boards, where conversion falls; the marginal rebound per added chance declines, so the mean response flattens for the top rebounders.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold: benching onset at 2 first-half fouls and 4-5 total
nonlinearities.why: Coaches bench bigs on a foul count, so the minutes loss from fouls is a step function of foul count rather than linear in the per-minute foul rate.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in dispersion: rung probability for 10+ rises faster than the mean when the pool variance is high
nonlinearities.why: Because the 10+ threshold sits in the upper tail for most players, doubling pool variance raises tail probability more than a proportional mean shift would.

contract.settlement_definition: Binary ladder: YES if the named player makes at least N three-pointers (floor_strike N-0.5, e.g. 5+ with floor 4.5) in the named game. Inactive or never-entering players settle at a fair price; once he enters, the market settles on actual made threes. Postponed games that start within 48 hours stay open, otherwise all markets resolve at a fair price. KXNBAESCALATOR3PT is scalar: payout floor(10000 x (y/10)^3)/10000 with y = min(10, s), so 10 or more made threes pays $1. The ladder, protected, every-game and ladder-style series in the ledger are TITLE_ONLY apart from KXNBA3PT and the escalator.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player enters the game the market settles based on the player's made three-pointers recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Standard threes ladder settles on actual made threes once the player enters; no early-exit protection.

rules_evidence.quote: Payout Formula = floor(10000 x (y / 10)^3) / 10000
rules_evidence.establishes: Scalar payout is cubic in made threes capped at 10; expected payout needs the full count distribution up to 10.

rules_evidence.quote: Each 1 made three-pointer increases the payout by the following schedule
rules_evidence.establishes: Payout schedule increments by each made three, from $0.0010 at one to $1.0000 at ten or more.

variants_and_edge_cases: Ladder rungs run 1+ to 7+; low rungs depend mostly on attempts>=1 and minutes, high rungs depend on the attempt tail and shooting luck, so the same player has different key drivers at different rungs.
Scalar escalator caps at 10 and weights counts cubically, so a 6-make night pays $0.2160 and 4 pays $0.0640; the expected value depends on the whole distribution between 3 and 8.
Protected (KXNBA3PTPROT) and every-game (KXNBA3PTALLGAMES) series are TITLE_ONLY: the protected refund branch and the multi-game conjunction cannot be specified from the sample.
Overtime is not addressed in the sampled text; official box score made threes normally include OT, adding about five minutes of attempts in about 6% of games.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box score made three-pointers as named in the full rules; the sampled secondary text is truncated before naming source agencies, so the exact source is unverified.

mechanism.summary: Made threes equal attempts times make probability. Attempts are minutes times a per-minute rate set by role (catch-and-shoot spot-up vs on-ball creator), the team's pace and who passes to him, modified by the score path (trailing teams launch more, leading teams bench shooters). Make probability is a context-weighted talent estimate (open catch-and-shoot vs contested pull-up) that is overwhelmingly noise in a single game, so the predictable component is attempts, and the make count is a thinned process whose variance exceeds a plain binomial because attempts and team-level shooting form are random. Settlement is the official count, with a cubic capped payoff in the escalator form. The main modelling hazards are role-specific minutes volatility for bench shooters and the dependence between a shooter's attempts and a specific passer's availability.

stages.name: Participation and minutes for a role player
stages.description: Spot-up shooters are often rotation players whose minutes change sharply with matchup, injury news and blowouts, so the minutes distribution is wide and sometimes zero-inflated for players on the edge of the rotation. Once he enters, the contract settles on his count, so brief appearances produce zero or one make.
stages.distribution: Wide mixture, zero- or low-inflated for fringe rotation players; bench minutes weakly dependent on game margin.

stages.name: Attempt rate given role and teammates
stages.description: Three-point attempts per minute reflect the shooter's role: off-ball spot-up players take 7-10 per 36 minutes mostly from passes, on-ball creators take pull-ups. The rate depends on who passes to him (passer availability) and who competes for the same looks, and on the team's pace and style. Attempt counts are overdispersed relative to Poisson because role and game flow change within games.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed count with variance exceeding mean (dispersion index about 1.3-1.8); mean attempt rate shifts by specific teammate absences.

stages.name: Defensive scheme and shot openness
stages.description: The opponent's scheme sets how many attempts are open or contested: drop coverage concedes above-the-break openings, switching and aggressive closeouts reduce them, and blitzing creates kick-out threes for the shooters. Openness affects both attempt volume and per-shot make probability, and it is a scheme trait rather than a luck outcome.
stages.distribution: Categorical scheme effect on both the attempt rate and per-shot make probability; effects of a few percentage points on make probability, 10-20% on attempts.

stages.name: Make probability: talent versus luck
stages.description: Given attempt context, each shot is a Bernoulli trial with probability depending on shot type and openness; single-game make rates are overwhelmingly luck and require heavy shrinkage (hundreds of attempts of prior). Team-level shooting form creates positive correlation across a team's shooters within a game, while player-level hot hands are statistically elusive.
stages.distribution: Sum of heterogeneous Bernoulli trials; per-game variance close to binomial with p near 0.36 plus a team-level shared shock; shrinkage weight depends on attempts.

stages.name: Game script effects on attempts
stages.description: Trailing teams take more threes late in the game and bench shooters gain minutes in blowouts, while starters who sit lose attempts; close games push closers to higher minutes. The net effect on a given shooter depends on role and on the margin path, which makes simple blowout penalties wrong for bench specialists.
stages.distribution: Path-dependent: attempt rate per minute is a function of margin bin and quarter; mixture over projected margin paths.

stages.name: Settlement form
stages.description: The ladder, protected and every-game forms are thresholds on one count (or a conjunction across games) while the escalator is a cubic expectation capped at 10; the same attempt-and-make distribution drives all but the relevant region differs. Official count with refund only for inactive players.
stages.distribution: Integer count with a right tail truncated at 10 for the escalator payoff; cubic weighting of counts 4-8.

nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.label: Hierarchical make probability by shot type (catch-and-shoot vs pull-up) and defender openness
nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.mechanism: Make probability depends on shot context more than on a single season 3P%, so talent should be estimated per context and recombined with tonight's expected context mix.
nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.rationale: Overall 3P% averages over open catch-and-shoot threes (about 38%) and tightly contested pull-ups (about 31%); a shooter's attempt mix changes with teammates and opposing closeouts, so the make probability changes even with fixed talent.
nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.measurement: Beta-binomial hierarchy on made/attempted by (catch-and-shoot, pull-up) x (wide-open, open, tight) cells over 3 seasons, league-cell mean as prior with prior weight 250 attempts per cell and player-level partial pooling; recent-season weight by 0.5 per year; combine cells with predicted tonight's context mix from shot-creation role and opponent openness allowed. Output a single p3 with credible interval. As-of: shots finished before tip.
free_sources: nba_api shot dashboards by closest-defender distance and type (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
raw_data: shot-level 3PA with type, defender distance, result
nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.why: Separates context-driven make probability from luck; the existing regression input shrinks a pooled 3P% instead.

nba.three_att_script_elasticity.label: Elasticity of a shooter's three-point attempt rate to score margin and quarter
nba.three_att_script_elasticity.mechanism: Trailing teams take more threes late and leading teams run clock and bench shooters, so 3PA per minute is a function of the margin path, not a constant.
nba.three_att_script_elasticity.rationale: Blowout dynamics cut starters but raise bench shooters' attempts; a close fourth quarter raises volume for closers; the sign differs between roles, so a single 'blowout' penalty misprices spot-up wings and bench shooters.
nba.three_att_script_elasticity.measurement: From play-by-play estimate per player 3PA per minute in margin bins (<-12, -12..-5, -5..+5, +5..+12, >+12) by quarter, with empirical-Bayes shrinkage to role-archetype bins (prior weight 120 minutes per bin); combine with the projected distribution of margin paths from team ratings (not the spread). Output expected 3PA integrating over the margin-path distribution and minutes mixture.
raw_data: PBP shot events with score margin, player minutes by bin
nba.three_att_script_elasticity.why: Captures role-specific blowout asymmetries that make bench shooters better, not worse, in lopsided games.

nba.assisted_three_passer_map.label: Share of shooter's made threes assisted by each teammate (passer dependence)
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.mechanism: A catch-and-shoot three requires a passer; the loss of a particular creator removes a specific fraction of assisted looks, with replacement playmakers delivering fewer.
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.rationale: Absence adjustments built from with/without splits ignore that dependence is concentrated in a few passers; in many pairs one creator generates 30-40% of a shooter's threes, so his absence matters far more than other absences.
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.measurement: From play-by-play assists, compute for each shooter the share of made+missed assisted threes by passer over 2 seasons (shrink shares to team-average share by prior weight 40 attempts); expected change in attempts = sum over passers of share x P(passer out) x (1 - replacement factor), replacement factor estimated from games the passer missed (default 0.65). As-of: injury report vintage.
raw_data: PBP: shooter, assister, made flag, shot type
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.why: Translates an injury headline into a number of lost assisted threes for each shooter.

nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.label: Opponent's rate of open and wide-open three-point attempts allowed (closeout quality)
nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.mechanism: A defense's effect on a shooter's threes shows up in the proportion of attempts that are open, which is a scheme trait and more persistent than opponent 3P% allowed.
nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.rationale: Opponent 3P% allowed mixes luck with scheme; the open-attempt share allowed and the opponent's volume allowed by shot type are stable within a season and map directly to a shooter's catch-and-shoot context.
nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.measurement: From tracking-derived shot data compute per defense the percentage of opponent threes taken with closest defender >= 4 ft (wide open) and 2-4 ft (open), the corner share allowed, and opponent 3PA allowed per 100 possessions; 60-game half-life, shrink to league mean with prior weight 40 games; match against the shooter's tonight's expected cell mix.
free_sources: nba_api defense dashboards by closest defender
raw_data: team defense shot dashboard: attempts by defender distance
nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.why: A stable, scheme-based replacement for the noisy position-allowed variable.

nba.minutes.reason: Attempts scale with court time and spot-up shooters have the most volatile minutes of any role; must be a scenario mixture because bench shooters swing between 8 and 28 minutes with matchup and injury news.

nba.three_volume.reason: 3PA per minute and catch-and-shoot share are the most predictive stable variables; the label bundles four different quantities (attempt rate, C&S share, 3P% shrinkage, opponent 3PA allowed) into one id and so cannot be audited or measured as stated.

nba.player_shooting_regression.reason: Heavy shrinkage of 3P% is the core of any threes model; value depends on using attempts-weighted shrinkage (about 750 attempts of prior), not a generic regression-to-mean factor.

nba.usage.reason: Usage is a weak proxy for three-point volume since spot-up shooters have low usage but high 3PA rate; useful only for the on-ball vs off-ball split.

nba.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Absence of passers lowers assisted-three share while absence of competing shooters raises attempts; direction depends on who is out, which this single label does not specify.

nba.opp_def_pos.reason: 3PA and 3P% allowed by position blends scheme with opponent shot-making luck and contains a large noise component at single-game scale; replace by contest-rate allowed.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Drop coverage concedes above-the-break threes and switching tightens them; useful when interacted with the shooter's catch-and-shoot share and with opponent closeout tendencies.

nba.three_pt_luck.reason: Team three-point luck regresses between games; shared team hot nights do create a within-game correlation among shooters, which is the real use.

interactions.mechanism: Expected threes are minutes times attempt rate times make probability, so minutes swings dominate for bench shooters whose attempt rate is high but whose minutes vary between 8 and 28; the same minutes error costs far more for a 9-attempt-per-36 shooter than a 3-attempt one.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose variance of threes into minutes, attempt-rate and make-rate components by role using player-game data and test that the minutes share is largest for bench shooters.

interactions.mechanism: The shrinkage weight on observed 3P% depends on cumulative attempts: a rookie with 150 attempts keeps little of a hot start while a veteran with 3000 attempts keeps most; recent form matters only for the low-attempt sample.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit predictive error of next-game 3P% using recent-form weight interacted with log career attempts and check that weight declines with attempts.

interactions.mechanism: A shooter's loss from an absent creator equals the share of his assisted attempts that creator generated times the shortfall of replacements; the effect is therefore concentrated in specific pairs rather than being a general absence penalty, and shooters with diversified passers are insulated.
interactions.how_to_test: For shooters with a dominant passer, compare attempts with vs without that passer; for diversified shooters expect near-zero effect.

interactions.mechanism: In a blowout the favorite's starters leave and bench shooters play expanded minutes with higher attempt rates, while the trailing team's shooters take more late threes; the sign of the effect of margin on threes depends on role, flipping between starters and bench specialists.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate 3PA per minute by margin bin for starters and bench separately; verify opposite slopes.

interactions.mechanism: Team-level shooting shocks (a hot night for the whole team) correlate the made-three counts of teammates; this does not change marginals but matters for parlays or when the same team's shooters appear on several rungs at once.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute correlation of made-three residuals between teammates over a season and compare with the independence benchmark.

nonlinearities.shape: convex tail: P(5+) rises faster than the mean attempt rate
nonlinearities.why: A threshold of five makes needs about 13 attempts at 36%; small increases in attempt rate move tail probability multiplicatively because 5+ sits far above the mean.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating: weight on recent make rate declines with attempt count
nonlinearities.why: Bayesian shrinkage gives a weight n/(n+k) on observed rate; with k near 750 attempts the weight on a 100-attempt sample is under 12%, so predicted make probability barely moves.

nonlinearities.shape: non-monotone in margin: attempts fall for starters, rise for bench and trailing team
nonlinearities.why: The effect of blowout probability on threes depends on role and on late-game urgency, giving a U- or inverted-U relation rather than a monotone one.
