contract.settlement_definition: Period contracts settle on points scored in a defined segment of the named game: quarter winner (YES if the named team outscores the opponent in that quarter), 'tie' markets (YES if neither team wins the quarter or half), spreads (named team wins the period by more than X.5), totals (combined points in the period above X.5) and team totals (one team's points in the period above X.5). Quarters 1-4 and the first half count only regulation points ('4th quarter markets do not include overtime'); the second half includes overtime ('2nd half markets are inclusive of overtime'). Postponement and void wording is not shown in the sampled period rules. Many series are TITLE_ONLY.

rules_evidence.quote: Note: Only points scored during the 1st half count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: First-half contracts count only first-half points, so overtime cannot enter them.

rules_evidence.quote: Note: Only points scored during the 2nd half (including overtime) count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Second-half contracts include overtime points, creating a wedge between 2H and Q3+Q4 regulation totals.

rules_evidence.quote: Note: 4th quarter markets do not include overtime.
rules_evidence.establishes: Quarter markets exclude overtime; the same standard note is printed on Q1-Q3 contracts.

rules_evidence.quote: If neither team wins the 1st quarter of the Miami vs Sacramento Pro Basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 8, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Period tie is a separate YES contract; winner markets therefore carry three outcomes with tie mass of about one in twenty.

variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime inclusion differs by contract: Q1-Q4 and 1H exclude OT, 2H (winner, spread, total) includes OT; a Q4 tie triggers OT which adds roughly 10-12 combined points to the 2H total but not to Q4.
Winner contracts have a tie leg (separate market 'tie in the 1st half/quarter'), so a model must produce a three-way probability, not a two-way split.

Sampled strikes are far from central values (e.g. 1st quarter total 71.5 and 2nd quarter total 70.5 versus a typical combined quarter score in the mid-fifties, 2nd half total 135.5 versus a typical ~110), consistent with listed ladders of rungs; strike construction and which rungs are live is not verified.
Spread strikes are half-points (7.5, 8.5), so no push exists; ties at zero margin go to the tie market (or NO for any team-win-by-X spread).
contract.settlement_data_source: Official game linescore / play-by-play scoring by period from the named league sources; the sampled period rules do not name the source agencies.

mechanism.summary: A quarter or half is a short scoring contest of roughly 24 possessions per team whose outcome is determined by who is on the floor in that segment, the number of possessions, efficiency per possession and small-sample noise, with score-state feedback across periods. The chain is: starters and rotation templates by quarter (Q1 and Q3 starters, Q2 bench-heavy, Q4 closers or garbage time), the period possession count (fast starts, slow lopsided Q4), unit-level offensive and defensive strength against the opponent's units, shooting variance that is large relative to a 24-possession sample, foul and bonus timing that resets each quarter, end-of-period shot-clock possessions, and the settlement rule (overtime excluded from quarters and first half, included in second half; ties pay a separate market). Because the sample is small, period margin is a noisy integer variable whose discreteness (ties, half-point cut points) matters, and most information comes from lineup identity and rotation structure rather than team-season averages.

stages.name: Lineups and rotation templates by quarter
stages.description: Coaches deploy starters for the first six to eight minutes, stagger substitutions into Q2, restart with starters in Q3 and then use closers or reserves in Q4 depending on score. Which five play in each period, and who is absent, determine the strength of the units. Starters confirmed shortly before tip are the most valuable late information for Q1 and Q3 markets; Q2 and Q4 depend on bench availability and coaching style.
stages.distribution: Discrete personnel states by quarter; the Q1 state is nearly deterministic after the starters are announced while Q4 is a mixture dependent on score.

stages.name: Period possessions and pace
stages.description: Possessions per period reflect both teams' tendencies and game state: fast early periods, decreased pace in lopsided late periods, long possessions at the end of a quarter. Period pace is not the game pace; each team's style and the identity of the units determine it, and totals markets scale with this count.
stages.distribution: Approximately normal around 24-26 possessions per team with sd about 2.5; correlated across the two teams and right-skewed by end-of-period shot-clock dynamics.

stages.name: Unit efficiency and matchup
stages.description: Each unit's points per possession against the opponent's units come from ratings of the relevant players, shot profile and defensive scheme. Opponent-adjusted ratings from full games blur unit differences, especially in Q2 and Q4, where bench-heavy units dominate. Matchup-specific mismatches (a bench big against a switching unit) matter more in short periods.
stages.distribution: Unit PPP roughly normal across units (sd of unit ratings about 6 per 100 possessions) with large sampling noise per period.

stages.name: Small-sample scoring noise and the margin distribution
stages.description: With about 24 possessions per team the sd of a team's quarter points is around five and the margin sd around seven; shooting luck therefore dominates and the probability mass at small integer margins (including the tie) cannot be treated as continuous. Hot starts regress rather than carry into later periods, so period luck is nearly independent across quarters.
stages.distribution: Discrete difference of two near-Poisson-binomial scores (Skellam-like) with excess kurtosis; tie mass of about 4-6% per quarter, higher in low-pace periods.

stages.name: Score-state feedback, halftime adjustments and foul resets
stages.description: Leads and trailing affect later periods: leading teams in the 2H may rest starters early, Q3 sees halftime adjustments, Q4 sees intentional fouling and clock management. Team fouls reset each quarter so bonus free throws cluster late in periods; end-of-quarter possessions and heaves shift totals. These effects are small for Q1 but central for Q4 and 2H markets.
stages.distribution: State-dependent mixture: Q4 and 2H are regime-switching with blowout versus close-game regimes; foul effects add right-skew to period totals.

stages.name: Settlement partitions and cross-market identities
stages.description: The contracts partition the game: Q1+Q2=1H, Q3+Q4 plus OT = 2H; OT is excluded from Q4 but included in 2H, and a Q4 tie triggers an overtime that adds roughly a dozen points to the 2H total. Period winners carry a tie outcome. Consistency across period totals and the game total is an identity, not a signal, and rule text defines which points count.
stages.distribution: Deterministic sum identities with a mixture over OT presence; OT occurrence probability about 5-7% conditional on regulation closeness.

talent_strength.note: Unit-level strength by quarter rather than full-game team ratings.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent units faced in each period, with scheme interactions at unit level.

role_personnel.note: Who plays each quarter is the central variable.

availability_news.note: Confirmed starters and absentees vintage matter for Q1/Q3.

coaching_scheme.note: Stagger patterns, Q3 adjustments and closing-unit decisions.

environment.note: Travel, altitude and rest may slow Q1 but effects are small; kept as context.

game_context_script.note: Blowout and close-game regimes for Q4/2H, and OT presence for 2H.

efficiency_conversion.note: Period shooting luck and unit efficiency.

distribution_variance.note: Discrete margin and total pmfs with tie mass.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and travel; weakly evidenced for period effects, and no motivation or clinch variable is included.

officiating_rules.note: Quarter-specific bonus and foul-reset mechanics and crew foul rates.

settlement_contract.note: OT excluded from Q1-Q4 and 1H, included in 2H, tie markets.

nba.quarter_unit_projection.label: Per-quarter expected on-court units and their projected net/offensive rating
nba.quarter_unit_projection.mechanism: Each quarter's scoring is the possession-weighted sum of ratings of the specific five-man units on the floor; coaches' stagger patterns make Q2 and Q4 weak or strong depending on who is available.
nba.quarter_unit_projection.rationale: Full-game ratings average over rotation; Q2 often features bench units with one starter, while Q1 and Q3 start with the best five. Because rotation patterns are predictable from coach tenure and are altered by injuries, a projection by quarter is a pregame-computable improvement over team ratings.
nba.quarter_unit_projection.measurement: For each team, build per-quarter minute-share matrix (player x quarter) from last 30 games with 15-game half-life, conditioned on starters confirmed and injury vintages; map to expected unit compositions; apply ridge-regularised lineup/player on-off ratings (lambda tuned by rolling CV) to compute expected points per 100 possessions in each quarter; adjust for opponent unit by the same method. Output: expected team points and margin per quarter with standard errors.
raw_data: stint and substitution data by quarter
lineup possessions and points
nba.quarter_unit_projection.why: Replaces team-season averages with the actual quarter-specific personnel, which is where period markets differ from the game market.

nba.period_margin_pmf.label: Empirical period-margin and period-total probability mass functions (ties, half-point cut points)
nba.period_margin_pmf.mechanism: Quarter margins are small integers with a sizeable mass at zero and at +/-1..3; winner, spread and total contracts cut this discrete distribution at specific points, so pmf shape (not only mean and sd) sets the probability.
nba.period_margin_pmf.rationale: A Gaussian approximation misprices tie mass (about 4-6% per quarter) and the probability of exceeding a half-point strike; the shape depends on pace (lower-possession periods have fewer scoring events) and on variance of the team-pair.
nba.period_margin_pmf.measurement: From all games in 5 seasons compute standardized period margin and total (actual minus rating-based expectation, built without market lines), fit a discrete mixture (Skellam-like with pace-dependent variance and a small-excess-kurtosis component) per period type (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, 1H, 2H-with-OT) via maximum likelihood with a team-pair variance covariate; report pmf at integer margins within +/-25 and the tie probability by expected pace tercile.
raw_data: linescore by period for each game incl. OT points
nba.period_margin_pmf.why: Directly gives tie probability for the winner contracts and exceedance probabilities at 7.5/8.5 margin strikes without relying on a normal approximation.

nba.period_foul_bonus_state.label: Team-foul and bonus-state exposure per period (foul reset each quarter, end-of-period fouling)
nba.period_foul_bonus_state.mechanism: Team fouls reset each quarter, so the shape of free-throw production within a period depends on when a team reaches the penalty, and Q4 end-of-period fouling adds free throws that distort Q4 totals and margins.
nba.period_foul_bonus_state.rationale: Free-throw volume per period differs from per-game rates because bonus onset is quarter-specific; crews that call more early fouls bring forward bonus situations in Q1/Q3, which can change period totals by 2-3 points; the effect is partly predictable from crew and team foul rates.
nba.period_foul_bonus_state.measurement: Compute team FTA per quarter and fouls per quarter from play-by-play over 2 seasons with 60-game half-life; estimate crew and team coefficients on quarter FTA via mixed model; project expected time-to-bonus in each quarter and expected FTA by period for tonight's matchup and crew; output expected FT points by period. As-of: crew assignment (announced game day) and team rates.
free_sources: nba_api playbyplayv3 foul and FT events
raw_data: PBP fouls and FTA by period
referee assignments
nba.period_foul_bonus_state.why: Period markets, unlike full-game markets, are sensitive to bonus timing because FT points cluster after the penalty begins.

nba.second_half_adjustment_effect.label: Coach-specific second-half and Q3 adjustment effect (Q3 efficiency minus game baseline)
nba.second_half_adjustment_effect.mechanism: After halftime coaches adjust schemes and starters re-enter, so Q3 scoring is not an average of Q1 and Q2 and certain coaches systematically outscore their baseline in Q3.
nba.second_half_adjustment_effect.rationale: Q3 and Q1 both start with starters but have different information sets; evidence of Q3 effects by coach is plausible but noisy; the quantity matters for Q3 winner/spread/total and for the 2H markets, and interacts with lead size.
nba.second_half_adjustment_effect.measurement: For each coach-team-season compute Q3 net rating minus first-half net rating regressed on margin at halftime and minutes played by starters in the first half; empirical-Bayes shrink across coaches (variance component estimated by method of moments) so that individual coach effects are heavily shrunk (typical shrinkage 80-90%); apply only when the coach is unchanged. As-of: games before tip.
raw_data: period net rating by team and halftime margin
nba.second_half_adjustment_effect.why: Provides the only structural reason for 2H/Q3 prices to differ from simple linear splits of full-game lines.

nba.period_possession_split.label: Possessions by quarter and team pace profile (fast early, slower late in lopsided games)
nba.period_possession_split.mechanism: Possessions per quarter vary by period (fast Q1, slower Q4 in decided games) and each coach has a pace style, so period totals scale with a period-specific possession count.
nba.period_possession_split.rationale: Applying game pace to a quarter overstates Q4 possessions in blowouts and understates Q1 for fast starters; the possession count times PPP is the correct decomposition for totals and team totals.
nba.period_possession_split.measurement: From play-by-play compute possessions per quarter per team with the standard possession formula (FGA - OREB + TOV + 0.44 FTA) by period for the last 2 seasons with 50-game half-life; model matchup period pace as weighted geometric mean with a slow-team weight of about 0.55 (estimate by regression); condition Q4 on pregame blowout-probability tercile. Output expected possessions per period and sd.
free_sources: nba_api box scores by period / PBP
raw_data: period-level FGA, OREB, TOV, FTA
nba.period_possession_split.why: Gives the period-specific volume term missing from the full-game pace input.

nba.starters_pit.reason: Confirmed starters, available about 30 minutes before tip, fix Q1 and Q3 personnel; the single most informative late-arriving variable for early-period markets, but only if the vintage is time-stamped relative to the order time.

nba.rotation.reason: Stint templates (when starters sit in Q1, Q2 staggering, Q4 closing unit) are what make each period different; too generic as written, it needs to be turned into expected on-court units per quarter.

nba.q_scoring.reason: Historical period scoring by team confounds lineup, opponent and game-script effects and uses small samples per team-quarter (about 80 games); as a standalone average it is mostly noise around full-game ratings, so only a shrunk period-specific deviation is useful.

nba.pace.reason: Period possessions drive total and team-total markets; but pace differs by quarter and is not the mean of two season paces, so a period-specific, lineup-aware version is required.

nba.off_rtg.reason: Full-game offensive rating mixes starters and bench; needs a starter-weighted version for Q1/Q3 and a bench-weighted one for Q2 to be informative.

nba.def_rtg.reason: Same issue as offensive rating; duplicates what an on-court-unit projection delivers once rotation is modelled.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: An absent starter changes Q1/Q3 more than the full-game average; vintage and confirmation timing matter.

nba.garbage.reason: Blowout probability matters for Q4 and for the 2H but is irrelevant for Q1; built from the spread it is a market observable and should be rebuilt from ratings.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Q4 fouling and clock are the key to Q4 totals and spreads and to end-of-quarter possessions in other periods; applies mostly to Q4 and 2H.

nba.score_resid.reason: Defined as residuals around market lines, so it is a calibration of the book not a driver; the required object is the raw period-margin distribution from scores, built without lines.

nba.three_pt_luck.reason: Hot starts regress; correct that a Q1 3P% outlier has no persistence into Q3, but this is a contextual caution rather than a predictor.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Slow-start-after-travel effects are small and unconfirmed for Q1; kept as context.

m.quote_history.reason: Price path is market state; useful to time when lineup news hit the quote, not a driver of period scoring.

m.rules_text.reason: Defines the split: Q1-Q3 and Q4 and 1H exclude overtime, 2H includes it, tie markets resolve YES when neither team wins; essential.

m.external_lines.reason: Labelled primary but is the sportsbook price; it is a benchmark to compare against, and using it as an input would copy the market rather than model periods.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-strike coherence is a quote-quality diagnostic; the sum-to-game-total consistency across periods is a useful arbitrage check but not a model input.

interactions.mechanism: Team Q1 history is valid only if tonight's starting five matches the historical one; a changed starter makes the stored Q1 rating stale, and the loss is larger for first and third quarters than for second and fourth, where the bench pattern matters more.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Q1 margin prediction error when the starting five is the modal five versus when one starter differs, holding team rating fixed.

interactions.mechanism: Second-half lineups depend on the first-half margin: when the margin exceeds roughly 15 at halftime coaches shorten Q3 starter minutes and use bench units in Q4, so Q3 and Q4 are two different regimes whose scoring rates differ in both pace and efficiency.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition Q3/Q4 total and margin on halftime-margin bins and test a break at |margin| near 15.

interactions.mechanism: Because 2H contracts include overtime and Q4 contracts do not, the 2H total is Q3 plus Q4 plus an overtime component with probability about 5-7% and size about 11-13 combined points, producing a right-skew in the 2H total and a wedge to Q3+Q4 prices.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose 2H total into regulation and OT parts in history and compare tail probabilities of the 2H total with and without the OT mixture component.

interactions.mechanism: Tie probability and margin variance both rise as possessions per period fall because fewer scoring events produce smaller margins; slow-pace matchups therefore have higher tie mass and lower probability of crossing 7.5/8.5 margin strikes.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin quarters by projected possessions and compare empirical tie frequency and exceedance rates at 7.5.

interactions.mechanism: End-of-quarter fouling when the team is in the bonus produces clusters of free throws at near-100% value; this convexly raises Q4 totals when the game is within 5 points, whereas early-quarter fouls matter less because bonus onset is later.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Q4 FTA and points per possession in the final two minutes by margin bin and team-foul count.

nonlinearities.shape: discrete, peaked at zero with excess kurtosis (Skellam-like)
nonlinearities.why: Winner, tie and spread-at-7.5 contracts cut a discrete integer distribution at specific points; a Gaussian approximation misstates tie mass and tail probability by 1-2 percentage points.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold: Q4 regime switch when margin exceeds about 15-18 entering Q4
nonlinearities.why: Starters are removed once the game is decided so Q4 pace and efficiency change discontinuously; effect on Q4 total and margin is small until the threshold.

nonlinearities.shape: step: effect of a missing starter on Q1 is larger than a proportional rating drop
nonlinearities.why: A missing starter changes all four teammates' lineup context in Q1 and also removes the scripted first-stint plays; the rating loss of the unit exceeds the player's marginal contribution.

nonlinearities.shape: concave: possessions saturate in fast periods while slow periods cluster tightly
nonlinearities.why: Pace is bounded by the 24-second clock so possession counts have limited upside but can drop sharply in lopsided Q4s.

contract.settlement_definition: No Kalshi series is filed under this archetype in the series ledger, so nothing can be read. By the catalog blueprint the targets are (a) race-to-N: the team (or possibly player) that first reaches N points in the game, and (b) game points leader: the player scoring the most points in the game. Overtime inclusion, the handling of co-leaders (equal points), DNP and void treatment, whether the race is team or player based, and the source of truth are all unverified; the closest live Kalshi series (KXNBARACE, KXNBAPTSLEADER) are classified under player_points and are TITLE_ONLY.
variants_and_edge_cases: Co-leaders: if two players score the same maximum, the contract may split, void or resolve to the first scorer; unknown without rules text, and with 20 players the probability of a tied maximum is roughly 5-8%.
Overtime: whether overtime points count toward the leader changes the result in about 6% of games and shifts probability toward the stars with highest minutes.

Race-to-N could be team-based or player-based (first player to N points); the ledger title 'NBA Race to Points' is ambiguous and the mechanisms differ (alternating-possession team process vs individual accumulation).

A race to N small enough to be reached in the first stint (5-15) depends on starters and first possession, while N of 30 or more reaches into the first-half rotation and behaves more like a half total.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not verifiable: no rules text exists for this archetype. Official play-by-play (for race timing) and box score (for leader points) would be the natural sources.

mechanism.summary: Race-to-N is a first-passage problem on two alternating-possession scoring processes with lumpy 0-3 point outcomes, so the winner is determined by who starts with the ball, the starters' first-stint scoring rates and the early-game noise, with the first-possession edge worth roughly half a possession and diminishing relative to noise as N grows. Points leader is the argmax over around twenty players' final points, driven by minutes (including overtime and blowout cuts), usage allocation within the unit, per-shot efficiency and a heavy-tailed scoring distribution, with negative dependence between teammates and positive dependence across teams through pace. Both contracts are winner-take-all functionals of the underlying scoring processes, so the tails and dependence matter far more than means, and settlement details (ties, overtime) change the answer materially.

stages.name: Opening conditions: tip, starters and first possession
stages.description: The race starts with the opening tip determining first possession and with the identity of the starters, confirmed only shortly before tip. The first possession is worth about half a possession in expected points, which is a large share of the total edge for small N and a minor one for N of 25 or more. Starter changes shift early scoring rates immediately.
stages.distribution: Binary tip outcome near 50/50 with weak team dependence; starters a discrete state known late; early scoring edge scales as the inverse of sqrt(N).

stages.name: Alternating-possession scoring dynamics
stages.description: Each possession ends in 0, 1, 2 or 3 points (with and-ones and free throws as lumps) and possession passes to the other team after a made field goal. The time to N points is a sum of lumpy renewals with correlation between teams induced by alternation, and per-possession efficiency of the starters against the opposing starters determines the winner.
stages.distribution: First-passage of two correlated renewal-reward processes with increments in {0,1,2,3}; overshoot and lumpiness matter at small N; the lead changes frequently.

stages.name: Participation and minutes of candidate leaders
stages.description: For the leader contract, each candidate's minutes are a mixture: full starter load, blowout trimming, foul trouble, early exit and overtime. The pool of plausible leaders shrinks to the top two to three scorers per team, so the minutes tail of those stars largely determines the winner.
stages.distribution: Mixture with left-tail and OT bump; the minutes of the top scorers are positively correlated with a close game.

stages.name: Shot allocation, efficiency and the tail of points
stages.description: Given minutes, a candidate's points depend on usage within the unit and shooting efficiency. Teammate absences concentrate scoring on fewer players and remove competitors for the title. Points distributions have a heavy right tail, so the maximum is often set by an outlier shooting night.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed, overdispersed points per player; negatively correlated within team given team total, positively across teams.

stages.name: Selection of the maximum and settlement
stages.description: The leader is the argmax over the candidate set; leader probability depends on the gap in expected points to the nearest rival and on the variance of each, and decays quickly with the gap. Ties, overtime and DNP handling are contract details that are not known here and shift probabilities materially.
stages.distribution: Winner-take-all functional (max of correlated heavy-tailed variables); probability concentrated in top few candidates; ties possible at integer maxima.

opponent_matchup.note: Opposing starters' defense in the first stint and rim protection facing the candidates.

role_personnel.note: Which five start and how scoring is allocated and correlated among the stars.

coaching_scheme.note: Opening play-calling (set plays for the first possession, early timeouts) and substitution timing of stars within the first stint are coach-specific, but no input in this archetype captures them.

environment.note: Neither contract has a venue-specific mechanism beyond what pace and starters already encode; home court has a small effect on early scoring and is absorbed in the race regression covariate.

game_context_script.note: Blowout trimming and OT affect leader; opening possession affects race.

nba.first_passage_race_table.label: Empirical race-to-N first-passage table by N, opening possession and early-game rating gap
nba.first_passage_race_table.mechanism: First-to-N is a first-passage problem on two alternating-possession scoring processes with lumpy increments; the answer depends on N, who has the ball first and the early-game scoring rate gap.
nba.first_passage_race_table.rationale: Treating the race as two independent Poisson clocks mispredicts because possessions alternate and scores come in 1-3 point lumps; the first-possession advantage is about half a possession and its relative value shrinks with N, so a table by N is needed.
nba.first_passage_race_table.measurement: From 5 seasons of play-by-play compute for each game and each N in {5,10,15,20,25,30} which team reached N first, whether that team had the opening possession and the starters' first-stint net rating gap; fit logistic regressions per N with covariates (opening possession, rating gap, home) and ridge shrinkage; output P(win race) with standard errors. Rating gap uses the first-stint rating below, not full-game rating.
raw_data: PBP scoring events with clock and team running totals
opening tip and possession
nba.first_passage_race_table.why: Gives the exact functional form of the race outcome as a function of N, so thresholds below 15 are not treated like game totals.

nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.label: Starting-five first-stint offensive and defensive rating and scoring-event mix
nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.mechanism: The race is decided in the first 4-8 minutes by the starters, whose joint rating differs from season team rating and depends on the exact five.
nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.rationale: Season team ratings average starters and bench; a starter-specific, first-stint rating (with set plays, shot mix and turnover rate) is the relevant strength and changes immediately if one starter is replaced.
nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.measurement: For each team compute points per 100 possessions and per-possession scoring-event distribution (0,1,2,3 points) for the first 8 minutes of games using the modal starting five over last 60 games (half-life 30 games), shrink to the team's full-game rating with prior weight 400 possessions; when tonight's starters differ, recompute via player-level on/off ridge ratings. As-of: starters confirmation time.
raw_data: lineup stints in first period with possessions and points
nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.why: Provides the strength variable at the right horizon and sensitivity to a single lineup change.

nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.label: Historical probability of being the game's top scorer by team scoring rank and usage gap
nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.mechanism: The leader is the maximum of about 20 players' points, concentrated among each team's top two or three scorers; the share a player has as leader depends on the gap in expected points to the nearest rivals, not on his own mean.
nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.rationale: Treating each player's points as independent normals overstates the chance of the second option and ignores that teammates' points are negatively correlated given team total; empirical leader shares by rank and gap calibrate the max-of-correlated-variables model.
nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.measurement: From 5 seasons of box scores compute for every player-game his rank among teammates by pregame expected points, the gap to the top rival in expected points, minutes and the indicator of leading both teams in points (with tie handling set per rule); fit a conditional logit on gap, team scoring concentration and OT; output P(leader) by rank-gap cell with empirical-Bayes shrinkage (prior weight 80 games per cell).
raw_data: player-game points, minutes, team and opponent identifiers
nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.why: Anchors the argmax model and shows how fast leader probability decays with expected-points gap.

nba.star_pair_scoring_correlation.label: Correlation of scoring between a team's top scorers and across the two teams
nba.star_pair_scoring_correlation.mechanism: Teammates split a roughly fixed number of shots so a big night for one lowers the other, while both teams share pace and officiating; this sets the covariance structure of the maximum.
nba.star_pair_scoring_correlation.rationale: Leader probability depends on the joint distribution: if two stars were positively correlated, the max would be less spread out than if negatively correlated; both are estimable from box scores.
nba.star_pair_scoring_correlation.measurement: Estimate residual-points correlation (actual minus minutes-conditional expectation) for each team's top-3 scorer pairs and for cross-team top-scorer pairs over 2 seasons using Fisher-z shrinkage to a league pair-type prior (prior weight 40 games); condition on co-star availability. Output a covariance matrix over the candidate set.
raw_data: player-game residual points
nba.star_pair_scoring_correlation.why: Required for the joint distribution that defines the maximum.

nba.starters_pit.reason: Opening five set the early scoring rates for the race and decide which stars are on the floor first; it is the most valuable late-arriving variable for the race, though the leader market needs full-game minutes more than the opening five.

nba.pace.reason: For race-to-N the relevant quantity is the possession rate of the first eight minutes, not the game pace; the existing definition is a full-game variable and will misrepresent early tempo.

nba.off_rtg.reason: A full-game offensive rating is a weak proxy for the starters' first-stint rating, which is what the race measures; useful only through the opening-stint version.

nba.def_rtg.reason: Same limitation as offensive rating: starter defense in the first stint is the relevant input; full-game values average over bench units.

nba.q_scoring.reason: First-quarter scoring history is the closest existing proxy for the race's early-game scoring rate, but it confounds lineups and opponents; shrink hard.

nba.tip_first_shot.reason: Opening possession matters materially for low N and decays with N; for the race this is a core input but the evidence for team-specific tip-off skill is thin, so the effect should be treated as a league-wide constant with weak team deviations.

nba.usage.reason: Shot shares are the main determinant of who leads the scoring; for the leader contract the usage of the top two scorers in each team and the gap between them is what matters, not the player's average usage.

nba.minutes.reason: The leader is typically the star with the most minutes; the tail of minutes (OT, blowout cuts) separates leaders and is a mixture variable.

nba.garbage.reason: Blowouts reduce the favorite's stars and raise the underdog's relative chances; the existing note is right but built from the spread it uses a market observable instead of ratings.

nba.ot_model.reason: Overtime adds scoring opportunity for stars and can flip the leader; but whether OT counts is not known (no rules), so it is context until the contract is read.

nba.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Absence of a co-star concentrates scoring and also removes a competitor for the leader title, an effect that is non-additive and large.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Star status vintage changes the leader candidate set outright; needs both teams' statuses.

m.quote_history.reason: A price path is market state, not a determinant of who scores first or most.

m.rules_text.reason: No rules text exists in the sample for these contract forms; tie, overtime and DNP wording for leader and race markets is the largest unknown and must be captured before any model is trusted.

m.external_lines.reason: Labelled primary but is the sportsbook price; benchmark for a fundamentals model, not an input.

interactions.mechanism: Race thresholds below 15 depend almost entirely on the identity of the starters and the opening tempo; a starter swap changes the scoring-event mix per possession, and the effect is largest when the replaced player is the primary creator.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare first-passage times to 10 points by starter-change indicator, controlling for opponent and opening possession.

interactions.mechanism: First possession is worth about half a possession in points; in a race to 5-10 it is a large share of the total edge but for N of 25 or above it is swamped by rating gap and noise, so the effect shrinks like 1/sqrt(N).
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the opening-possession coefficient separately for each N in the logistic race model and check the decline.

interactions.mechanism: When a co-star sits the top scorer's expected points rise and a rival for the leader title disappears, so the leader probability grows faster than the usage gain alone; the effect on the opposing team's best scorer is the opposite.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare leader share of a star in games with and without his top teammate, holding opponent and minutes.

interactions.mechanism: Overtime favors the highest-minutes stars while blowouts remove the favorite's stars; leader probability therefore switches between a star-dominated regime in close games and a bench-diluted regime in lopsided ones.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate leader share by star team win-probability bin and OT indicator.

interactions.mechanism: Negative same-team correlation in points lowers the chance of both teammates scoring high, so the maximum is often a single outlier; positive cross-team correlation via pace increases both sides' high tails, spreading leader probability across teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate max with the observed covariance vs independent marginals and compare to realised leader frequencies.

nonlinearities.shape: convex/softmax-like: leader probability rises faster than expected points gap
nonlinearities.why: The maximum of several heavy-tailed variables gives winner-take-all behavior; a player with a modest expected-points edge over the second option wins disproportionately more often because the field is split among many low-probability candidates.

nonlinearities.shape: decaying like 1/sqrt(N) in the race threshold
nonlinearities.why: First-possession advantage is a roughly constant half possession of points while the standard deviation of the margin at N points grows with N, so the probability edge declines with N.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise with an OT step and blowout truncation
nonlinearities.why: Stars' minutes jump by about five in OT games and are cut in lopsided games, making leader probability a discontinuous function of projected game closeness.

contract.settlement_definition: Season-long contracts for 2026-27: champion/conference/Finals outcomes, Cup champion, win-total thresholds (KXNBAWINS: YES if the named team wins at least N regular-season games, strike_type greater_or_equal), regular-season records and streaks, award-type contracts (Finals MVP, conference finals MVP, social justice champion) and viewership. Regular-season-only series exclude preseason, playoffs (including the play-in) and the All-Star Game; NBA Cup games before the Cup final count as regular season. When several teams or players tie for a result the 'Yes' side pays $1/N (rounded down to the cent). Most series are TITLE_ONLY; rules were sampled for five series.

rules_evidence.quote: If the Utah Pro Basketball team wins at least 60 games in the 2026-27 regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Win-total contract counts regular-season wins only with a greater_or_equal strike, so playoffs and the play-in are excluded.

rules_evidence.quote: NBA Cup games before the Championship game are part of the regular season and do count towards a winning streak.
rules_evidence.establishes: Cup group and knockout games before the final count toward regular-season streaks and standings; contradicts the existing cup_format note.

rules_evidence.quote: Only regular season games count.
rules_evidence.establishes: Streak markets exclude playoffs, play-in, All-Star game and the Cup final.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple players are awarded,
rules_evidence.establishes: Award contracts split payout $1/N among multiple winners, so co-winner probability matters.

rules_evidence.quote: If Washington is the Emirates 2026 Pro Basketball Cup champion in the 2026-27 season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Cup champion contract resolves on the Cup final winner of the 2026-27 season (single-elimination knockout).

variants_and_edge_cases: Ties for the longest streak or the best record pay $1/N: a tied streak of 14 among two teams pays each $0.50, so the contract is on the distribution of the longest streak and the number of tied teams, not just one team's streak.
KXNBAWINS uses greater_or_equal at integer strikes, so a push does not exist; a team finishing exactly at the strike resolves YES.
Cup games count as regular-season games except the championship game, so Cup group results enter win totals while the Cup final does not.

Award-type contracts (Finals MVP, conference finals MVP, social justice champion) are determined by voting panels and carry multiple-winner payout rules; finals viewership series resolve on audience figures and are not outcome-driven.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league standings and results for win totals/streaks; league announcements for awards and Cup winners; viewership by published audience figures. The sampled text does not name the specific source agencies.

mechanism.summary: Season-level team contracts are functionals of a simulated season: a latent team strength (a prior from the roster plus in-season updates, with real uncertainty), the realized availability of its stars over the games and into the playoffs, the remaining schedule with home/away and rest, game results as correlated Bernoulli trials giving a Poisson-binomial win total, standings with official tiebreakers and the play-in structure, and then a playoff bracket of best-of-seven series with tightened rotations. Probabilities of rare outcomes (title, 60 wins, longest streak) are convex in uncertainty: errors in rating sd and star health matter more than error in the mean, and boundary effects at tiebreaks and seed cut points drive seed contracts. Award, Cup and viewership contracts add functionals (voting conditional on team result, single-elimination knockout, audience) that have their own mechanisms.

stages.name: Latent team strength: prior and in-season update
stages.description: True strength before the season is a roster-based prior (minutes-weighted player impact, aging, continuity, rookies), with an error sd of roughly 3-4 net rating points. Each game updates it with a gain that declines with games played; with ten games played the prior still dominates. Trades and coaching changes shift both mean and variance with a lag for integration.
stages.distribution: Gaussian posterior with sd about 2.5-3.5 net rating points early in the season shrinking with games; heavy tail for roster shocks (trades, injuries to stars).

stages.name: Availability of stars over the season and into the playoffs
stages.description: Stars miss a random number of games through injury and load management, with a heavy right tail of long absences; the quantity that matters differs by contract: expected games missed for win totals and seeds, probability of being healthy in April-June for round-reach and titles. Availability changes the team rating by a player-specific amount.
stages.distribution: Mixture: most players miss 5-15 games, a few percent miss most of the season; time-to-injury is a survival process with age and workload dependence.

stages.name: Schedule: opponent strength, rest, Cup structure
stages.description: The remaining schedule determines each game's win probability through opponent strength, home/away and rest asymmetry; Cup group games count as regular-season games while the final does not. Early in the season schedule effects are small compared with rating uncertainty, but they matter for the final-weeks seed battle.
stages.distribution: Deterministic schedule given; game win probabilities range 15-85%; the rest/travel adjustments are about +/-1 point of margin.

stages.name: Regular-season win totals and streaks
stages.description: The win total is a sum of correlated game outcomes: independent Bernoulli noise (sd about 4.5 wins for an average team) plus common shocks through rating uncertainty and injuries, making the win-total distribution wider than a binomial. Longest-streak and best-record markets are extremes over thirty teams of run-length and total processes, with a heavy tail in the hot-streak regime.
stages.distribution: Poisson-binomial with a hierarchical shock (total sd about 6-7 wins); extreme-value behaviour for longest streaks; ties pay 1/N.

stages.name: Seeding, tiebreakers and play-in
stages.description: Seeds and division winners are determined by win totals plus the official tiebreak hierarchy; the play-in structure further changes who makes the playoffs and who enters as which seed, and some Kalshi seed contracts are defined before the play-in. Boundary probabilities depend on ties, which depend on head-to-head and division/conference records.
stages.distribution: Discrete rank outcomes with ties; probability at boundary seeds is sensitive to a one-win difference and to tiebreak procedure.

stages.name: Playoff bracket and series conversion
stages.description: Each series is a best-of-seven with home-court structure, playoff-tightened rotations and game-to-game correlation; per-game win probability converts steeply to series probability. The bracket path (who a team meets) and star health in each round give the round-reach and title probabilities, which are strongly convex in team strength.
stages.distribution: Series win probability is an S-shaped function of per-game edge (60% per game gives about 71% series); correlation between games from injuries and adjustments widens outcomes.

stages.name: Derived award, Cup and audience functionals
stages.description: Finals and conference-finals MVP contracts are conditional on team success times the voting share of its best player; the Cup champion is a single-elimination knockout in a neutral venue after group play; viewership contracts depend on which teams reach the Finals and on series length. Each derived contract has its own mechanism layered on the team simulation.
stages.distribution: Conditional-choice (multinomial logit) for awards; single-elimination bracket for the Cup; regression with year effects for audience.

nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.label: Preseason team prior from minutes-weighted roster impact with aging curves and continuity
nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.mechanism: A team's true strength before and early in the season is a function of who is on the roster, how those players age, and how much of last year's unit returns; this prior dominates for the first 20-30 games.
nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.rationale: With about ten games played, the 2026-27 rating is mostly the prior; building it from last season's team rating ignores offseason roster churn, aging and rookie contributions, and the error of the prior sets the uncertainty of every futures contract.
nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.measurement: Prior team rating = sum over projected rotation of (expected minutes share x player impact projection), where projection = last-two-season blended impact (weights 0.6/0.3/0.1 over 3 seasons) + aging adjustment by age bucket (estimated from historical year-over-year change; roughly +1.0/-0.3/-1.0 per 100 possessions at ages 22/28/33) + continuity adjustment (minutes-weighted share of returning players, coefficient estimated by backtest); shrink to league mean by sd of prior error estimated from 10 historical seasons; report mean and sd. As-of: before opening night and updated at each roster transaction.
free_sources: EPM / RAPM published by Dunks&Threes or similar
raw_data: player-season impact ratings, ages, minutes, team rosters, transactions
nba.preseason_roster_aging_prior.why: Provides the quantified prior and its sd, which the existing rating input only asserts.

nba.rating_update_gain.label: In-season rating update gain and posterior sd (how fast current results override the prior)
nba.rating_update_gain.mechanism: True team strength is updated game by game with weight given by signal-to-noise; the gain declines with games played, and calibrating it by backtest sets how fast futures should move.
nba.rating_update_gain.rationale: A rating that overweights early results (10 games) swings futures; under-weighting leaves stale priors. The right gain is estimated from past seasons and depends on whether margin or win/loss is used and on roster stability.
nba.rating_update_gain.measurement: Backtest across the last 15 seasons: regress end-of-season margin per game on preseason prior and games-played-weighted current margin; solve for optimal weight w(n) as a function of games played n (expect w near 0.2 at n=10, 0.5 at n=40); posterior sd of true rating = sqrt(prior_var x (1-w)); use margin of victory capped at 15 and garbage-time excluded. As-of: all games before the as-of date.
raw_data: team-game margins, possessions, rosters by game
nba.rating_update_gain.why: Converts the generic 'rating with uncertainty' into time-varying numbers for every season-level contract.

nba.tiebreak_ledger.label: Head-to-head, division and conference record ledger for tiebreaker evaluation
nba.tiebreak_ledger.mechanism: Seeds and division winners are decided by the league's tiebreak hierarchy (head-to-head, division winner, conference record and so on), so exact ties are resolved by information that accumulates over the season.
nba.tiebreak_ledger.rationale: Simulating only win totals misses the probability that a tie is broken in a team's favor; at seed boundaries (6th vs 7th, 10th vs 11th, play-in cutoff) a tie occurs in about 8-15% of final standings and the tiebreak ledger is partly known before the season ends.
nba.tiebreak_ledger.measurement: For each team pair compute season-to-date head-to-head wins/losses and remaining games, division record, conference record and record vs playoff teams, updated nightly from game results; in the simulation, apply the official tiebreak procedure (stored as code from league rules) to simulated ties and output P(win tie) by pair. As-of: nightly after final scores.
raw_data: game results by pair, schedule, division/conference identifiers
nba.tiebreak_ledger.why: Needed for division winner, seed over/under and playoff qualifier contracts where ties decide outcomes at boundaries.

nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.label: Time-resolved probability that each rotation star is healthy for each playoff round
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.mechanism: Title and conference odds are convex in star availability, and the relevant availability is in April-June, not the regular-season games-missed average.
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.rationale: Games-missed expectations average over a season; the quantity that matters for round-reach contracts is the probability of being healthy at tip of each playoff series, which depends on current injury state, history, age and minutes load.
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.measurement: For each player in the top-3 of each contender estimate a hazard model for an injury ending availability (survival model by age, previous-season games missed, minutes per game, current injury status) fitted on 10 seasons of injury data; output P(healthy at playoff start), P(healthy for round k) conditional on being healthy at the start; combine with team-level strength loss from the player's absence (impact x minutes share). As-of: injury report vintage.
raw_data: injury episodes with start/return dates, player minutes, ages
nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.why: Converts star health into a probability mixture for the series simulation, which is what makes title odds convex.

nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.label: Probability a given player wins Finals/Conference Finals MVP conditional on his team winning the series
nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.mechanism: Award contracts are conditional on the team winning and then on voter choice among its players, which follows stat shares and narrative in the series.
nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.rationale: Finals MVP of a champion usually goes to the top scorer or best player of the series, with media voters weighing series scoring, efficiency and team role; P(player MVP) = P(team wins) x P(player chosen | team wins) and the second factor can be estimated from past award results.
nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.measurement: From 20 seasons of Finals and Conference Finals results compute for each champion's top-3 players the share of MVP awards by rank in series points, by pre-series team star ranking and by minutes share; fit a conditional logit on pre-series expected points rank and best-player indicator (pre-series BPM rank), regularised; output P(MVP | team wins) by player. Combine with series win probability from the series model. As-of: before series start (updated per game).
raw_data: award results, series player stats, pre-series ratings
nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.why: Required for KXNBAFINALSMVP, KXNBAWFINMVP, KXNBAEFINMVP and KXNBAMVPCHAMP contracts that sit in this archetype.

nba.finals_viewership_drivers.label: Finals viewership drivers: market sizes, star power, series length and Game 7 incidence
nba.finals_viewership_drivers.mechanism: A viewership threshold contract depends on the matchup's audience size (markets, stars), series length and number of games, and the broadcast measurement method rather than on team strength alone.
nba.finals_viewership_drivers.rationale: KXNBAFINALSVIEWER and KXNBAFINALSVIEWERGAME7 settle on audience counts; these are functions of which teams reach the Finals, how many games are played and the rating baselines of past years; they are not outcomes of basketball production but of audiences.
nba.finals_viewership_drivers.measurement: Regress average Finals viewership on the log combined TV market size of the two teams, a star-power index (number of all-NBA/All-Star players), series length and prior-year trend over 15 seasons (use published Nielsen figures as released by the broadcaster); add year effects for measurement changes (out-of-home viewing, streaming) and forecast with a prediction interval. As-of: before the Finals, updated by conference-finals outcomes.
free_sources: Sports Media Watch / press releases of Nielsen ratings (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for completeness)
raw_data: Finals average viewers by year, teams, series length, market sizes
nba.finals_viewership_drivers.why: Without it the two viewership series in this archetype have no input list at all.

nba.ratings.reason: Team rating is the backbone of every futures contract; the existing text promises a preseason prior and uncertainty but gives no way to compute either, and in-season updating weights are unspecified.

nba.lineup_adj_rating.reason: Availability-adjusted strength is what projects the rest of the season; for futures it must be integrated over the distribution of who plays, not evaluated at tonight's active set.

nba.player_impact.reason: Player-level impact values are the way to project a team after trades and injuries; subject to aging and role-change error, and noisy for rookies and new acquisitions.

nba.standings_sim.reason: The simulation is the actual evaluator for win totals, seeds, play-in and round reach; value depends on the tiebreaker implementation and on drawing correlated rating shocks across teams.

nba.sos_remaining.reason: Remaining schedule strength matters for win-total and seed markets mid-season; early in a season (about ten games played) it is a minor effect compared with rating uncertainty.

nba.pythag_residual.reason: Wins above point-differential expectation partly regress; but clutch luck is mostly noise so the weight on it should be small and estimated from backtests.

nba.injury_risk_season.reason: Star availability distribution drives title convexity; but it needs to be time-resolved (probability healthy in April) not just games-missed expectation.

nba.load_mgmt.reason: Rest policy for stars lowers regular-season wins in a known way; matters for win-total and seed markets but not for playoff-only contracts.

nba.title_path.reason: Bracket path and home-court structure matter for round-reach and title; modest compared with team strength except for specific matchups.

nba.series_model.reason: Best-of-seven conversion of per-game probability to series result is central to all playoff round markets and is strongly non-linear in the per-game edge.

nba.playoff_rotation.reason: Playoff minute concentration raises star-heavy teams' strength relative to regular-season ratings; effect size is modest (a few percent of net rating) but systematic.

nba.news.reason: Trades and coaching changes are event signals that move rating and uncertainty with a lag; useful as triggers, but the quantity needed is a re-estimate of rating, which is player-impact driven.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Rest and travel effects are tiny at the season-aggregate level and are already in schedule-aware ratings; including them as a season-futures input mostly double counts.

nba.cup_format.reason: The attached reason says Cup games do not affect regular-season standings, which contradicts the rules text sampled for KXNBATEAMWINSTREAK ('NBA Cup games before the Championship game are part of the regular season and do count'); the Cup champion contract needs the knockout structure but the standings claim must be corrected.

m.quote_history.reason: Futures price path measures information arrival and staleness; a market series, not a team-strength driver.

m.rules_text.reason: Rules differ across the 31 series: regular-season-only streaks with Cup games counted, tie payouts of 1/N, award contracts with split payouts, pre-play-in seed definitions.

m.external_lines.reason: De-vigged sportsbook futures are the consensus benchmark; including them as an input would reproduce the market.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Coherence across win-total and seed rungs is a quote-quality check; a simulation's own ladder is monotone.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Depth limits tradable size on thin futures books; execution realism only.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: With one season per label the realised hit-rate history is too thin to calibrate rare events, and it is a label set not a driver.

m.fees.reason: Fee schedule and capital lockup affect expected return of long-dated positions, not the probability of the event.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: Favorite-longshot bias in the Kalshi futures book is an overlay on model probabilities; it is not an input to team strength.

interactions.mechanism: Title and conference probability are convex in team strength and in star availability: a healthy-star scenario multiplies title odds several-fold while the injured scenario nearly eliminates it, so the correct estimate is a mixture over star-health states, not the rating at the mean health.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare title probability from a mixture over star-health states with that from average rating; check calibration on historical contenders.

interactions.mechanism: Seed and division contracts flip at exact ties; teams within one win of a cutoff have probabilities controlled by the tiebreak ledger (head-to-head, division record), which is a discontinuous rule on top of continuous win totals.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the share of simulated seed outcomes decided by tiebreakers and the sensitivity to head-to-head ledger perturbations.

interactions.mechanism: Early in the season the posterior is dominated by the prior; as games accumulate the weight shifts to results. The optimal weighting depends on roster continuity: teams with many new players update faster because the prior is less reliable.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest end-of-season margin against prior and current margin separately for high- and low-continuity teams.

interactions.mechanism: Playoff rotation tightening raises star-heavy teams' strength in exactly the games that decide titles, so the bracket path matters differently for deep teams versus top-heavy ones; a bracket in which a deep team faces a star team early changes round probabilities beyond the rating difference.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate playoff net rating minus regular-season net rating by roster concentration and test its interaction with opponent type.

interactions.mechanism: A trade changes team strength and uncertainty with a lag of 10-20 games because the integration of a new player lowers early effectiveness; the rating update should widen variance at the time of the trade and then narrow.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare team net rating in games 1-10 versus 11-30 after a major trade relative to the player-impact prediction.

nonlinearities.shape: steep S-shape: series win probability versus per-game win probability
nonlinearities.why: Per-game probability of 55% gives about 61% series, 60% gives about 71% and 65% gives about 80%, so small rating differences are amplified by the best-of-seven structure.

nonlinearities.shape: logistic around threshold-like contracts: P(60+ wins) as a function of mean wins
nonlinearities.why: With a win-total sd of about 6-7 the probability of reaching 60 moves from about 5% at 52 expected wins to 50% at 60 wins, and the slope is largest near the strike.

nonlinearities.shape: convex/mixture: title odds jump discretely when the star is healthy in the playoffs
nonlinearities.why: Title probability is not linear in expected games missed; it depends on a bimodal health state at playoff time, and losing the top star removes most title chance for a top-heavy team.

By blueprint the targets are season records (team or player marks), season stat leaders (who leads points, rebounds, assists and so on at season's end), player streaks (consecutive games meeting a threshold) and specials. Which games count, qualification minimums, whether a DNP breaks a streak, tie payouts and the source of truth are all unverified; related live series (KXNBASTATAVG, KXNBAPLAYERHIGHSCORE, KXNBAWINSTREAK) are filed under the unregistered counting-specials archetype.
variants_and_edge_cases: Leader markets may apply or waive a games-played qualification (the neighbouring KXNBASTATAVG states that league minimum thresholds do not apply, but this archetype has no rules of its own); the choice flips the effect of injuries from a cliff to a smooth average.
Streak markets differ on whether a game missed (inactive) breaks the streak, is skipped or voids the contract; the product-of-probabilities approximation is wrong for any of these.
Ties for a leader title or record may pay 1/N or resolve by a tiebreak; with per-game averages rounded to one decimal, ties at the displayed figure are common.
Regular-season-only versus including playoffs and the play-in changes totals and averages materially; unknown without rules text.
contract.settlement_data_source: Unverified: official NBA statistics (NBA.com / league data partners) are the natural source but no rules text exists for this archetype.

mechanism.summary: Season stat markets are long-horizon aggregates of game-level production, with outcomes decided by three layers: (1) how many games each candidate plays (injury, load management, qualification rules), (2) the player's per-game rate trajectory (minutes, usage, role changes with age and teammates), shrunk toward a preseason projection, and (3) the aggregation form: an average (variance falling as 1/sqrt(n)), a maximum over candidates (leader race with correlated candidates), a run-length process (streaks broken by absences) or a team record (head-to-head-linked wins). The existing catalog treats this as one family; the mechanism differs materially across forms, and the dominant uncertainty is availability rather than per-game talent. Rules (qualification minimums, tie payouts, what breaks a streak) can turn a smooth process into a cliff.

stages.name: Games played and qualification
stages.description: The number of games a candidate plays is a random variable with a heavy right-hand mass near the full schedule and a left tail from injuries and load management; qualification rules turn this into a cliff or a smooth effect depending on the contract. Rest decisions concentrate in the second half for older stars and around eligibility thresholds.
stages.distribution: Mixture: most players play 65-78 of 82 games, with a long left tail; hazard rising with age and previous-season absences; cliff payoff at the qualification threshold.

stages.name: Per-game rate trajectory
stages.description: A player's true per-game rate is a function of minutes, role, usage and age, which evolves through the season with teammates' availability and coaching decisions. Observed averages to date are noisy estimates of the true rate; shrinkage toward a preseason projection prevents overreaction to early results.
stages.distribution: Gaussian posterior for the true rate with sd shrinking with games played; role shocks (injuries to teammates) produce jumps.

stages.name: Aggregation into averages and leader races
stages.description: A season average has sampling variance falling with the number of games, so late-season leaders are mostly decided; a leader contract is the maximum over candidates whose averages are correlated through shared opponents and, for teammates, through shared possessions. The probability of leading is a function of the gap, the remaining games and each candidate's qualification probability.
stages.distribution: Maximum of correlated Gaussian-ish averages with sd shrinking in remaining games; probabilities decay rapidly with the gap; ties at rounded displayed figures possible.

stages.name: Streak and run-length processes
stages.description: A streak contract is a run of consecutive games meeting a threshold, with per-game hit probability set by minutes and opponent and a break if the player misses a game (rule dependent). The probability of a run of N is far from a simple power of the average hit probability because hits are persistent within stretches and absences cause breaks.
stages.distribution: Run-length distribution of a Markov process with state-dependent hit probability; right-skewed with absorbing breaks.

stages.name: Team records and special season outcomes
stages.description: Team record contracts depend on a simulated season where head-to-head games link teams' results and rating uncertainty is common; the maximum over teams and tie handling define outcomes. The simulation also gives winning-streak and best-record probabilities.
stages.distribution: Extreme-value behaviour over thirty correlated Poisson-binomial win totals; ties possible at integer totals.

talent_strength.note: Player rate posterior and team strength for records.

opponent_matchup.note: Season-long averages and records wash out single-opponent effects: the schedule's opponent mix enters through schedule strength in the simulation rather than through matchup-specific variables, so no matchup input is needed at this horizon.

role_personnel.note: Role and minutes trajectory, redistribution when teammates miss time.

availability_news.note: Games played distribution and qualification probability.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching changes that alter a star's role, minutes cap or rest policy are not quantified by any input in this archetype's list; the effect on a season stat leader could be large mid-season.

environment.note: Venue and altitude effects average out over 82 games and do not matter for season totals or streaks beyond what pace and team ratings capture.

game_context_script.note: Single-game script effects like blowouts are averaged over the season and are absorbed in per-game rate and minutes; no separate script input is required for season-level markets.

pace_volume.note: Team pace and the player's per-game volume as a trajectory.

efficiency_conversion.note: Regression of early hot streaks in shooting-dependent stats toward talent.

distribution_variance.note: Variance of averages, run-length distributions and cross-team covariance.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest incentives near eligibility thresholds and schedule density.

officiating_rules.note: Official qualification rules and tiebreak procedures for stat titles (minimum games, minutes, how ties are shown) are changing and not versioned in any input; the exact criteria for the current season is not captured.

settlement_contract.note: Qualification, streak definition and tie handling; unknown here.

nba.stat_rate_posterior.label: Shrunk posterior of a player's true per-game stat rate given games to date and preseason projection
nba.stat_rate_posterior.mechanism: A season-long average or leader race depends on the player's true rate, which is a weighted combination of the preseason projection and the noisy to-date average.
nba.stat_rate_posterior.rationale: Early-season averages overstate hot starts; the weight on results needs to be calibrated per statistic (scoring is more stable than rebounding and assists), and the posterior variance determines how much the leader gap is worth.
nba.stat_rate_posterior.measurement: Prior mean = preseason projection (last-two-season blend with aging adjustment); weights by stat: n_prior of about 25 games for points, 35 for rebounds, 40 for assists (to be estimated by backtest of ten seasons); posterior mean = (n_prior x prior + n x observed)/(n_prior + n) with minutes-conditional adjustment; posterior sd = sqrt(per-game variance/(n_prior + n)). As-of: games to date.
raw_data: player-season per-game stats, minutes, ages
nba.stat_rate_posterior.why: Provides the leader-gap state in correct units, rather than raw season totals.

nba.qualification_probability.label: Probability a candidate meets the contract's qualification rule (games, minutes, or none)
nba.qualification_probability.mechanism: Leader and award-like markets require a minimum number of games or minutes; a player's chance depends on the distribution of games played and on strategic rest near the threshold.
nba.qualification_probability.rationale: A scoring leader who misses 25 games might be disqualified under a minimum-games rule or still counted if the rule says qualification thresholds do not apply; this is a cliff in the payoff and varies by contract.
nba.qualification_probability.measurement: For each candidate compute P(games_played >= G_min) where G_min is read from the contract (or 0 if 'qualification thresholds do not apply'): games played = games to date + Binomial-like process over remaining games with per-game availability from an injury-hazard model and a load-management multiplier for players >30 or with a history of rest; record probability and the conditional leader probability given qualification; update after every game.
raw_data: games played, remaining schedule, injury history, ages
nba.qualification_probability.why: Turns the static eligibility rule into the cliff probability that moves leader markets.

nba.streak_hit_persistence.label: Game-to-game persistence of threshold hits and streak-break hazard (DNP, rest, matchup)
nba.streak_hit_persistence.mechanism: A streak of N games meeting a threshold is a run-length process whose per-game hit probability varies with minutes and rest and which is broken by any DNP or rest night.
nba.streak_hit_persistence.rationale: Treating hits as independent with the season-average rate understates both streak and break risk; minutes and rest dependencies create positive autocorrelation within a stretch, and the specific rule (whether inactive games break the streak) changes everything.
nba.streak_hit_persistence.measurement: For each player estimate a logistic model of threshold hit on minutes projection, rest days, opponent defensive rating and lag-1 hit (to capture persistence beyond minutes) over a 3-season window; compute probability of a run of length at least N via a Markov chain with state = current run length and per-game hit probability from the model; add break hazard per game from injury/rest model. Adjust for the rule on inactive games (counts as break, skip, or void).
raw_data: player-game stats and minutes, availability flags
nba.streak_hit_persistence.why: Gives the actual structure of consecutive-game contracts, where the product of per-game probabilities is the wrong approximation.

nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.label: Dependence between teams' records via head-to-head games and conference schedule overlap
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.mechanism: Records of contending teams are not independent: when two top teams play each other, one gains what the other loses, and shared opponents create correlation in schedule luck.
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.rationale: Best-record and most-wins markets are about the maximum over teams, so the covariance of wins across teams matters; ignoring head-to-head linkage and common opponents misstates the extreme's distribution.
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.measurement: From the remaining schedule compute pairwise numbers of head-to-head games and common-opponent overlap; in the simulation draw correlated team-strength shocks and enforce zero-sum head-to-head results; estimate the covariance of final win totals across the top-8 contenders by simulation; output distribution of the maximum and the probability of ties (tie handling per rule). As-of: nightly.
raw_data: schedule of games with teams, results to date
nba.team_record_head_to_head_linkage.why: Needed for record and winning-streak contracts of any team vs the league.

nba.season_stat_pace.reason: Current totals and per-game trajectory are the state variable of a leader race; but raw to-date averages must be shrunk toward a preseason projection, otherwise a 10-game hot start dominates.

nba.minutes.reason: Minutes per game is the dominant driver of per-game counting stats and changes with injuries, age and coach; needs a trajectory rather than a single projection.

nba.usage.reason: Role stability determines scoring per game, but for assists and rebounds leaders usage is far less relevant than touches or rebound chances; mislabelled as primary-level driver of all stat races.

nba.injury_risk_season.reason: Games played is the biggest source of variance in who leads a season stat; the existing label is a games-missed expectation, whereas qualification contracts need a distribution of the number of games played.

nba.load_mgmt.reason: Rest policy lowers games played and minutes for older stars and interacts with eligibility rules; moderate effect, concentrated in the second half.

nba.games_played_eligibility.reason: Eligibility thresholds convert availability into a cliff for leader markets; as a rule description it is static and needs conversion to a qualification probability.

nba.stat_dist.reason: Game-level distributions matter for streak probability and for the variance of a season average; the effect on leader probability is secondary to the number of games.

nba.standings_sim.reason: A team simulation is what team-record markets (best record, streaks) require; for individual stat leaders it is only context.

nba.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Role shifts when teammates miss time affect rates, but the season-level horizon makes a game-by-game with/without split second-order.

nba.ratings.reason: Team strength matters for team record markets; for player stat leaders it affects pace and blowout minutes only slightly.

m.quote_history.reason: A price series reflects information arrival; it is a market observable not a driver of stat totals.

m.rules_text.reason: Qualification minimums, streak definitions (does a DNP break the streak), tie payouts and rounding are the contract; no rules text exists for this archetype so it must be captured.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: With one label per season per contract realised hit-rate history is too thin for calibration of rare events; context only.

interactions.mechanism: The probability of leading is a mixture over the number of games the candidate plays; a small current gap matters less than the chance that the leading player misses time, so leader probability falls faster than a gap-based normal calculation implies.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute leader probability from a model with random games played vs fixed games and compare calibration on historical season leaders.

interactions.mechanism: A minimum-games rule creates a cliff: players near the threshold are managed (rested or played through minor injury) to qualify, so expected games played is not independent of the rule; the effect is concentrated in the last 10-15 games.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare rest rates in the final 15 games by distance to the eligibility threshold.

interactions.mechanism: A streak probability is the product of per-game hit probabilities, which depend on minutes; a small minutes shortfall in one game breaks the streak, so streak probability is highly sensitive to the minutes tail rather than to the mean rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate per-game hit probability by minutes bucket and compute the streak probability by Markov chain versus the average-rate power.

interactions.mechanism: Best-record and most-wins contracts depend on the maximum over linked teams; head-to-head games reduce the variance of the maximum for teams in the same conference compared with independent teams, so ignoring linkage overstates the chance of an extreme winner.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate maxima with and without head-to-head linkage and compare against historical distribution of the best record.

interactions.mechanism: A teammate's long-term injury switches the player's role regime for the rest of the season, changing the posterior mean and variance at once; to-date averages from the earlier regime are misleading.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit rate models with a regime indicator for key-teammate absence and compare predictive error with and without it.

nonlinearities.shape: cliff at the games threshold
nonlinearities.why: The payoff for a leader depends on meeting a minimum number of games, so the probability of leading jumps when a player's expected games cross the threshold; the response is a step smoothed by availability uncertainty.

nonlinearities.shape: exponential decay in run length (geometric) with minutes-dependent hazard
nonlinearities.why: The probability of N consecutive hits decays roughly as p^N, with p itself dependent on minutes; small errors in p are amplified exponentially in N.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating: weight on observed average rises as n/(n+n_prior)
nonlinearities.why: The influence of to-date results on the posterior mean follows a hyperbolic shrinkage curve, so early-season changes in average move the estimate little and late-season changes move it a lot.

contract.settlement_definition: The live series under this archetype are playoff-advancement-type contracts rather than series winners: seed thresholds (KXNBASEED and KXNBASEEDOU: YES if a team's regular-season conference seed is at or better than the stated seed, determined at the end of the regular season and before the play-in), playoff qualifier, play-in membership and advancement, 1-seed contracts, home playoff games, an undefeated playoffs team, playoff triple-double, Cup qualifiers and group winners, and draft-order contracts (lottery top 3, draft top 5 to 30 picks). Only KXNBASEEDOU has sampled rules; all other series are TITLE_ONLY.

rules_evidence.establishes: Seed contracts resolve on the end-of-regular-season conference seed, not the post-play-in seed.

rules_evidence.quote: its seed for this market is still 10
rules_evidence.establishes: Worked example in the rules: a team finishing 10th that wins the play-in and enters as the 8 seed still counts as 10, so '#8 seed or better' resolves No.

rules_evidence.quote: If the Washington Pro Basketball team is the #10 seed or better at the conclusion of the 2026-27 Pro Basketball regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
