variants_and_edge_cases: Seed contracts use the pre-play-in seed while playoff qualification and 'play-in advance' contracts depend on the play-in games; the same team can have very different probabilities across these series.

Draft contracts (KXNBADRAFTTOP5..30, KXNBATOP3, KXNBATOP5ROTY) concern lottery outcomes and player slots, which depend on pick ownership, protections and the combinatorial lottery, not on playoff series.
Cup contracts (group winner, qualifier) depend on group tiebreakers including point differential; Cup games before the final count as regular-season games per other Kalshi rules in this sport.

Rare-event aggregator series (undefeated playoffs team, playoff triple-double, home playoff games) are functionals of the bracket simulation with their own distributions, and the home-games series may or may not count play-in games.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league standings (conference seed at regular-season end), lottery results, Cup standings and box scores; the sampled seed rules do not name the data provider.

mechanism.summary: These contracts are not best-of-seven winners; they are functionals of three structures laid on a simulated season. The first is the final regular-season standing distribution (team strength with uncertainty, availability, schedule, tiebreaks) giving seeds, qualification, 1-seeds and the play-in set; the second is the format machinery applied to it (play-in bracket, lottery combinatorics with pick ownership and protections, Cup group tiebreaks including point differential); the third is the playoff bracket simulation generating counts such as home games, undefeated runs and triple-doubles. The outcome therefore depends on rule-accurate simulation more than on a single rating, with boundary effects at ties and cutoffs, and the existing catalog's series-winner focus misses the draft, Cup-group and counting products entirely.

stages.name: Final regular-season standing distribution
stages.description: Each team's final record is a sum of game outcomes with rating uncertainty, injuries and schedule, and the seed is its rank within the conference. Seed thresholds like 'the 10 seed or better' are cut points on this rank distribution, with ties common near boundaries. Late-season rest and tanking incentives alter results for teams that have clinched or been eliminated.
stages.distribution: Rank distribution derived from a hierarchical Poisson-binomial simulation; probability at boundary seeds sensitive to a single win.

stages.name: Format rules: seeding definition, play-in and tiebreaks
stages.description: The contract defines seed as the end-of-regular-season conference seed, so the play-in changes qualification but not the seed. The play-in bracket maps pre-play-in seeds 7-10 into the playoff field through games with specific home-court structure; tiebreakers decide equal records. The same simulated standings produce different answers for qualification, seed-over/under and play-in contracts.
stages.distribution: Discrete rule-based mapping; the play-in is a three-game mini-tournament with per-game win probabilities near 50%.

stages.name: Draft order: lottery and pick ownership
stages.description: Draft position for non-playoff teams follows a combinatorial lottery with fixed odds by pre-lottery rank, and the pick may be owned, swapped or protected by another team. Player-slot contracts (top-20, top-10, top-5) add a prospect board layer and the possibility of trades. These contracts use the same standing distribution but a different mechanism.
stages.distribution: Known combinatorial lottery (e.g. 14% top-pick odds for each of the worst three); protections give kinked, conditional ownership; prospect rank to slot is noisy.

stages.name: Cup group stage and knockout
stages.description: Cup group winners and qualifiers are determined by group record and tiebreakers (including point differential), and the knockout stage is single-elimination. Teams' incentives in the last group games depend on the standings state, and margin matters for tiebreaks. Cup games before the final count in the regular season record.
stages.distribution: Small group tables with discrete outcomes; margin enters via the tiebreak; knockout rounds are single games with win probability near rating-implied values.

stages.name: Playoff bracket and counting products
stages.description: Given the bracket, series lengths and advancement drive the count of home games, the chance of an undefeated run (four consecutive sweeps) and the number of games in which a player can record a triple-double. These are functionals of the series simulation with correlation across games from injuries and adjustments.
stages.distribution: Series length distribution (4-7 games), probability of an undefeated run is a product of sweep probabilities (very small), triple-double aggregator is a 1 - E[(1-p)^G] over player games.

talent_strength.note: Team strength with availability for standings and bracket; prospect talent for draft handled via the board.

opponent_matchup.note: Bracket matchup and series conversion for playoff-count contracts; Cup group opponents by schedule.

role_personnel.note: Stars' playoff minutes and the triple-double candidates.

availability_news.note: Star availability vintages for seed, qualification and series.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach-specific playoff rotation shortening, tanking decisions and Cup tiebreak management are not represented by an input in this archetype; coaching effects on the late-season standing are unquantified.

environment.note: Home-court and travel structure inside series and the Cup.

game_context_script.note: Margin distribution for Cup tiebreak and game-to-game correlation in series.

pace_volume.note: Possession counts are irrelevant for these advancement, draft and count contracts beyond their contribution to team ratings; no pace or volume variable has independent explanatory value.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shooting efficiency regression matters inside team ratings but these contracts depend on standings and format outcomes; no stand-alone efficiency input improves them.

distribution_variance.note: Series length, lottery draw, home-games pmf and rare-event aggregators.

officiating_rules.note: Format rules: play-in, Cup tiebreakers and lottery odds (rules, not referees).

settlement_contract.note: Seed definition before the play-in, draft ownership and protections.

nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.label: Draft lottery combinatorial odds by pre-lottery rank, including ties and the four-pick rule
nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.mechanism: Pick position for non-playoff teams is a random draw with fixed odds by rank (worst three teams each 14.0% for the top pick, no team falling more than four slots), so draft-position contracts reduce to rank odds times a rank distribution.
nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.rationale: Draft top-3/top-5/top-10 contracts are decided by the lottery, which is a known combinatorial mechanism; the uncertainty is the pre-lottery rank (final record, ties, coin flips) and the team's pick ownership, not the draw itself.
nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.measurement: Encode the current lottery's 1,000 (or 14 x ...) combination allocation by rank 1-14, compute exact P(pick k | rank r) for k=1..14 (including the rule that teams cannot fall more than 4 positions and ties in record are broken by random drawing before the lottery); combine with the simulated distribution of final regular-season ranks from the standings simulation (include play-in losers) to get P(top-3 pick | team). As-of: nightly; rules versioned by draft year.
raw_data: lottery combination table, simulated final ranks, tiebreak random draw rule
nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.why: Gives an exact component for KXNBATOP3 and the draft-pick-range series, instead of treating them as team strength outcomes.

nba.pick_ownership_ledger.label: Pick ownership, swap and protection ledger (who holds each first-round pick and conditions)
nba.pick_ownership_ledger.mechanism: A team's lottery position and a player's draft slot depend on who owns the pick, on swaps (the better of two picks) and on protections that roll or convey only above a rank.
nba.pick_ownership_ledger.rationale: Contracts on a team's draft position or a player's slot are about picks, which may be owned by another team, swapped or protected; a model based on the team's own record will misattribute the outcome.
nba.pick_ownership_ledger.measurement: Build a table by draft year with (original team, current owner, protection threshold (e.g. top-8 protected), swap condition, rollover year, second-round pick conveyance) from public transaction records; in simulation, determine each pick's final owner and slot after draw; maintain nightly updates for trades; validate against NBA.com list of draft picks. As-of: transaction dates.
raw_data: trade records with protections and swap terms
nba.pick_ownership_ledger.why: Without it a top-N pick contract can be mis-mapped to the wrong team.

nba.play_in_path_model.label: Play-in bracket path probabilities given pre-play-in seed and relative strength
nba.play_in_path_model.mechanism: The play-in tournament maps seeds 7-10 to final seeds 7 and 8 through a fixed bracket, so the playoff qualification and the post-play-in seed differ from the regular-season seed; Kalshi's seed contracts are measured before the play-in.
nba.play_in_path_model.rationale: KXNBASEEDOU resolves on the regular-season seed before the play-in while qualification/play-in series depend on play-in outcomes; the same team has different probabilities for 'seed 8 or better' depending on which definition applies.
nba.play_in_path_model.measurement: Encode the bracket (7v8 winner gets the 7 seed; 9v10 loser is out; loser of 7v8 plays winner of 9v10 for the 8 seed), compute per-game win probabilities with home-court from team ratings and rest, and convolve to P(final seed 7, 8, out | pre-play-in seed, opponents); estimate the distribution of opponents from the standings simulation. As-of: nightly; rules versioned by season.
raw_data: standings, play-in format, team ratings
nba.play_in_path_model.why: Required to separate pre-play-in seed contracts from qualification contracts for the same team.

nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.label: Distribution of the number of home playoff games by seed and path
nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.mechanism: A team's total home playoff games is the sum over rounds of home games in each series, which depend on home-court status (seed), series length and advancement.
nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.rationale: KXNBAPLAYOFFHOMEGAMES and KXNBAPLAYOFFHOST count games rather than winners; probability mass depends on the series-length distribution (4-7 games) and on losing in an early round with few home games.
nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.measurement: For each team and round compute P(reach round) from the bracket simulation, P(home-court) from the seed comparison, and the distribution of home games in a series given length and home status (2-2-1-1-1: 4,3,3,2 or 2 for lower seed... enumerate); convolve across rounds into a pmf of total home games; include play-in home games if the contract counts them (unknown). As-of: nightly during playoffs.
free_sources: Computed from the series model and NBA schedule format
raw_data: bracket simulation outputs, series format
nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.why: Directly constructs the target pmf for the home-games series.

nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.label: Cup group standings state with point-differential tiebreak and remaining-games simulation
nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.mechanism: Cup group qualifiers are decided by group record then tiebreakers (head-to-head, point differential and so on), so the state is a table with a margin component that rewards running up scores in some games.
nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.rationale: Group-winner and qualifier contracts depend on remaining games, but also on margin of victory in each game because the point-differential tiebreak influences outcomes; a win/loss-only simulation misses this.
nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.measurement: From the Cup schedule compute standings, point differential and head-to-head results to date; simulate the remaining group games with margin distributions from team ratings (sd about 13 points per game) and apply the official group tiebreak order and wildcard rule to produce P(group winner), P(qualifier by wildcard); update after each Cup game. As-of: nightly; rules versioned by season.
raw_data: Cup schedule, results with margins, tiebreak order
nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.why: Needed for KXNBACUPQUAL and KXNBACUPGROUP contracts, which sit in this archetype.

nba.playoff_triple_double_rate.label: Per-player playoff triple-double rate given expected games and minutes
nba.playoff_triple_double_rate.mechanism: A playoff triple-double contract is an at-least-one-event over the playoffs; probability depends on the few players with triple-double production, the expected number of playoff games each plays and their playoff minutes.
nba.playoff_triple_double_rate.rationale: KXNBAPLAYOFF3D cannot be priced from regular-season rates alone: minutes rise for stars, games depend on series length and advancement, and triple-double rate per game is concentrated in a handful of high-assist bigs and guards.
nba.playoff_triple_double_rate.measurement: For each candidate compute P(triple-double | game) from regular-season rate adjusted by playoff minutes factor (starters about +2 to +4 minutes) with shrinkage to a role prior (weight 20 games); expected games from the bracket simulation as a distribution; P(at least one TD in playoffs) = 1 - E[(1-p)^G]; aggregate across candidates with correlations through team advancement. As-of: nightly.
raw_data: player-game triple-double flags and minutes; bracket game-count distribution
nba.playoff_triple_double_rate.why: Supplies the rare-event aggregator needed for the playoff triple-double series.

nba.series_model.reason: Needed for home-playoff-games, undefeated and playoff triple-double contracts that live in this archetype; game-to-game correlation and series-length distribution are the useful parts, but none of the sampled series is a series winner.

nba.lineup_adj_rating.reason: Availability-adjusted strength helps late-season seeding and playoff series; for draft-pick and Cup-group contracts it is only indirectly relevant.

nba.ratings.reason: Team strength drives seed, qualification, 1-seed and cup group outcomes; the playoff-adjusted version mentioned is not defined and regular-season ratings need rotation-concentration adjustment for series.

nba.playoff_rotation.reason: Playoff minutes tightening matters for series and for playoff triple-double markets (stars' minutes rise); irrelevant for draft and Cup contracts.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Star availability moves seed, qualification and series odds; the vintage and expected return timeline are central.

nba.venue.reason: Home-court worth about 2-3 points per game is the sole structural asymmetry in the series and determines home playoff games; a fixed constant plus team-specific deviations, small.

nba.cup_format.reason: Cup group qualifier and group winner contracts are decided by the group tiebreak hierarchy and wildcard rules; but the input is a rule description and has to be turned into a state-aware simulation.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Rest between games in a series and Cup travel are second-order next to rating and availability; the series home/away pattern already encodes most of it.

nba.standings_motivation.reason: Tanking and clinch/rest incentives are the mechanism behind late-season seed and draft-position contracts, and they are sparse and hard to measure; keep with partial knowability.

nba.title_path.reason: Bracket path matters for 1-seed and home playoff games but is only a context for draft and Cup contracts.

nba.score_resid.reason: Defined as a residual around market lines, which makes it a book calibration; the Cup point-differential tiebreak needs the raw distribution of single-game margins from scores, not a residual vs lines.

m.quote_history.reason: A price path measures information arrival, not draft order or series outcomes.

m.rules_text.reason: Seed contracts are defined before the play-in ('Results of Play-In games do not affect the outcome'); the exact definition changes the probability, and the other series rules are unknown.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook futures are the consensus comparison; not inputs to a model.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Coherence across seed thresholds (e.g. #10 or better, #8 or better) is a quote-quality diagnostic; model ladders are monotone by construction.

interactions.mechanism: A star injury during a series makes later-game outcomes positively correlated, so independent-game models overstate sweep probability and the chance of an undefeated run; a healthy and an injured regime have different per-game probabilities and the lengths differ accordingly.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the distribution of series length conditional on a star injury during the series with an independent-game model.

interactions.mechanism: Lottery odds apply to the team that owns the pick after protections and swaps; a protected pick may convey only if it lands outside a rank range, so the probability of a team landing a top-3 pick is conditional on ownership and rank jointly, producing kinks at the protection boundary.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute pick conveyance probability from simulated ranks and protection terms and compare with contract prices for teams with protected obligations.

interactions.mechanism: Teams near the 6-7 and 10-11 boundaries have incentives that change in the last games (avoid the 7-8 game, avoid the 10 seed), which makes win probabilities in the final week depend on the standings state; the play-in structure creates thresholds in the value of one win.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the dependence of late-season win probability on the standings state and on the play-in value of marginal wins.

interactions.mechanism: Group tiebreakers on point differential give incentives to run up scores in some games and rest stars in others; the value of margin is non-linear because it matters only if the team ends tied on record, and the probability of a tie depends on the state of the group.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the group with and without margin-based tiebreaks and compare qualification probabilities; check late-game garbage-time scoring when the margin matters.

interactions.mechanism: Total home games is a convex function of advancement because deep runs add rounds each with up to four home games, while early exits produce few; the distribution is right-skewed and its mean is dominated by the probability of reaching the third and fourth rounds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated home-games pmf by seed with historical outcomes.

nonlinearities.shape: kinked, non-monotone in rank: equal odds for the worst three, steep decline afterwards
nonlinearities.why: The top-pick odds are flat for ranks 1-3 and fall by rank thereafter, with a hard rule on maximum fall; the relationship between record and pick position is therefore not smooth.

nonlinearities.shape: product structure: undefeated-playoffs probability is a product of four sweep probabilities
nonlinearities.why: Each sweep needs about 60-80% for the favorite, so the product is a few percent; small errors in per-game probability multiply across 16 games.

nonlinearities.shape: logistic with ties: seed-threshold probability near cutoffs
nonlinearities.why: The probability of reaching 'seed 6 or better' is a steep function of expected wins near the boundary, with ties broken by rule making it step-like at integer win totals.

contract.settlement_definition: Binary ladders on one player's official counts in the named game: blocks at or above N (e.g. 3+ blocks, floor_strike 2.5), steals at or above N (3+ steals) and combined steals plus blocks at or above N (4+, floor 3.5). Inactive players and players who never take the court settle at a fair price; once a player enters, the market settles on his recorded steals/blocks/combination. A postponed game that starts within 48 hours stays open, otherwise all markets resolve at a fair price. No turnover series is present in the ledger despite the archetype name; overtime treatment is not stated in the sampled text.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player enters the game the market settles based on the player's blocks recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Block ladder settles on actual blocks once the player enters; no early-exit protection.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player enters the game the market settles based on the player's steals recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Steal ladder settles on actual steals once the player enters.

rules_evidence.quote: This market resolves based on the number of combined steals and blocks recorded by Day'Ron Sharpe.
rules_evidence.establishes: Stocks contract counts the sum of steals and blocks, so the dependence between components matters.

variants_and_edge_cases: Strike construction: the sampled rungs are tails for the named players (Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 3+ blocks, Jrue Holiday 3+ steals), i.e. low-probability events in the 3-8% range, so dispersion and credit noise dominate the mean.
Combined stocks (4+, floor 3.5) is a sum of two overdispersed counts; the right-tail probability depends on the covariance and on archetype (a rim protector's stocks are mostly blocks).
Turnovers (the archetype name includes them) have no live series in the ledger, so a turnover contract's rules (assist-to-turnover, team turnovers) are unverified.
Overtime is not mentioned in the sampled rules; official box score steals and blocks normally include OT minutes, adding about five minutes in about 6% of games.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box-score steals and blocks as named in the full rules; the sample is truncated before naming source agencies, so the exact source and correction policy are unverified.

mechanism.summary: Steals and blocks are rare counts (typically 0-3 per game) generated by a Poisson-like event process whose rate is the product of minutes, the supply of opportunities and the defender's conversion: steals need live-ball turnovers by opponents and the defender's deflection activity; blocks need opponent rim attempts while the defender is the rim anchor and his contest-to-block conversion. Both are overdispersed because supply varies by opponent style and lineup and because minutes are a mixture, and both carry an additional layer of noise from official-scorer credit decisions. At strikes of 0.5, 1.5 and 2.5 the probability depends more on dispersion and the tail of supply than on the mean, and the stocks contract sums two counts with archetype-specific dependence. The existing catalog uses generic matchup variables; the dominant missing pieces are hustle-based deflections, rim-protector supply, and the sum dependence.

stages.name: Participation and minutes mixture
stages.description: Low-count events scale with court time, so the minutes mixture sets the rate: a blowout cuts the starter's minutes but may raise bench players' attempts to press, and foul trouble affects aggressive defenders. Early exits settle on actual counts because the contract voids only inactive players.
stages.distribution: Mixture over minutes scenarios; the effect on a Poisson rate is multiplicative and dominates at the 2.5 strike.

stages.name: Supply of blockable shots and stealable turnovers
stages.description: Blocks require opponent shots at the rim contested by the player; the supply is the opponent's rim frequency while the player is on court and his share of contests. Steals require live-ball turnovers by opponents, with supply set by the opponent's careless handlers and style. Pace scales both supplies but is second-order to the opponent's shot and turnover mix.
stages.distribution: Supply counts overdispersed relative to Poisson with team-pair dependence (e.g. rim attempts per game vary with sd about 5 around a mean near 28).

stages.name: Defender conversion: deflections, contests and scheme
stages.description: The defender converts opportunities at a stable personal rate: steals per deflection and blocks per contest, modulated by scheme (blitz and zone raise deflections, drop coverage anchors the center near the rim). Rates are persistent but samples are small, so shrinkage towards role priors is needed.
stages.distribution: Thinned Poisson per opportunity with player-specific rates; sampling noise dominates a single-game count.

stages.name: Credit noise and dependence for stocks
stages.description: Official scorers decide steal and block credit, with arena-level tendencies and post-game video review corrections, which adds dispersion at the 0.5/1.5 strike. The stocks contract adds steals and blocks whose dependence differs by archetype: activity-driven for versatile wings, nearly independent for rim anchors.
stages.distribution: Count noise inflated by credit decisions (extra dispersion index 0.1-0.2); bivariate dependence with archetype-specific correlation 0-0.3.

stages.name: Threshold crossing and settlement
stages.description: The ladder rung is a threshold on an integer count with a small mean, so the probability of 3+ is a tail event highly sensitive to the dispersion assumption: a mean of 0.9 blocks gives 3+ probability of roughly 5% under Poisson and noticeably more with overdispersion. Settlement uses the official box score and refunds only inactive players.
stages.distribution: Tail of a negative binomial with mean 0.5-3; rung probabilities highly convex in the dispersion parameter.

nba.deflection_rate.label: Deflections and steal-conversion rate per 36 minutes (hustle stats)
nba.deflection_rate.mechanism: A steal is a conversion of a deflection or a pass interception; deflections are a more stable measure of defensive activity than steals and predict future steals better than past steals do.
nba.deflection_rate.rationale: Steal counts are 0-3 per game with huge sampling noise; a player's deflection rate and his conversion rate (steals per deflection) separate persistent skill from luck and respond to scheme (gamble-heavy teams generate more of both).
nba.deflection_rate.measurement: Compute deflections per 36 minutes and steals per deflection from hustle-stat tracking for the last 2 seasons with 45-game half-life; shrink conversion to league mean (about 0.20 steals per deflection) with prior weight 80 deflections; expected steals per minute = deflection rate x shrunk conversion; adjust for opponent live-ball turnover propensity. As-of: games before tip.
free_sources: nba_api hustle stats (leaguehustlestatsplayer, game-level boxscorehustlev2; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for per-game availability)
raw_data: hustle: deflections, steals, minutes per game
nba.deflection_rate.why: Gives a stabler, scheme-aware rate for the 0.5/1.5/2.5 steal rungs than season steals per minute.

nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court.label: Opponent rim attempts faced while the player is the on-court rim protector, and contest/block rate
nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court.mechanism: Blocks equal opponent rim attempts faced times the player's contest share times block rate per contest, so block supply depends on who is the anchor and how many shots the opponent takes at the rim while he is on court.
nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court.rationale: Total FGA or team pace is a poor supply measure: a drop-coverage center faces 20+ rim attempts, a switching center fewer; opponent rim frequency while the player is on court, and the share of contests that are his, move block expectation more than his season blocks per minute.
nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court.measurement: From tracking and play-by-play compute per player: opponent rim attempts per 36 minutes on court, contest share (his contests / team contests), block rate per contest (shrunk to role prior with weight 150 contests); project tonight's rim attempts faced = opponent rim FGA per 100 possessions x possessions while on court x anchor-minutes share. Include position-pair changes when another rim protector is out. As-of: tip.
free_sources: nba_api defensive dashboard (shots defended at rim, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for per-game)
raw_data: defense dashboard: DFGA at rim, contests, blocks; lineup minutes
nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court.why: Gives the supply side of blocks with the relevant matchup, which pace and total shots miss.

nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.label: Opponent live-ball turnover rate and primary handler carelessness
nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.mechanism: Steals mostly come from live-ball turnovers (bad passes, dribbles stripped); the opponent's rate of live-ball versus dead-ball turnovers and the quality of its primary handlers set steal supply.
nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.rationale: Total opponent turnovers per game include offensive fouls, shot-clock and out-of-bounds events that cannot be stolen; the live-ball share and the primary handler's turnover rate are the supply for the steal contract.
nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.measurement: From play-by-play classify opponent turnovers as live-ball (steal-credited or bad-pass) or dead-ball; compute live-ball turnovers per 100 possessions for the opponent over last 40 games (half-life 20), shrink to league mean with prior weight 20 games; add the turnover rate of the expected primary ball handlers (from lineup) and adjust for opponent's pace. As-of: injury report.
raw_data: PBP turnover types, steal credit, lineups
nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.why: Targets the portion of opponent turnovers that a defender can steal.

nba.stocks_dependence_by_archetype.label: Dependence between steals and blocks for combined stocks, by player archetype
nba.stocks_dependence_by_archetype.mechanism: Combined steals+blocks sums two counts whose dependence depends on defensive archetype: wings with deflection-based steals and bigs with rim blocks have small correlation, while versatile defenders have positive correlation through minutes and activity.
nba.stocks_dependence_by_archetype.rationale: The 4+ stocks rung needs the distribution of the sum; assuming independence or perfect minutes-driven correlation misstates variance, and the covariance is archetype specific.
nba.stocks_dependence_by_archetype.measurement: Compute the within-player correlation of steal and block counts after controlling for minutes (Pearson on Pearson residuals) over 3 seasons by archetype (guard, wing, forward, center), with Fisher-z shrinkage to archetype mean (prior weight 60 games); model sum distribution via bivariate negative-binomial or Gaussian copula with these parameters; output P(S+B >= k) for k=2..6.
raw_data: player-game steals, blocks, minutes
nba.stocks_dependence_by_archetype.why: Provides the dependence parameter needed for KXNBASTOCK that the independent components cannot.

nba.minutes.reason: Low-count events scale with court time; for blocks the minutes that matter are those alongside particular opponents' rim attackers, and a blowout cut matters little at a 0.5 strike but a lot at 2.5.

nba.steal_block_rates.reason: Per-minute rates are stable for blocks and moderately stable for steals; but the label bundles the player's own skill with opponent turnover and rim-attempt rates, which should be separated to be measured.

nba.turnover_pressure.reason: Ball-handling load and opponent pressure are the two halves of turnovers; deflections are the best proxy for pressure but need a hustle-stat source; no turnover series appears in the ledger, so this input mostly serves steals through opponent carelessness.

nba.usage.reason: Touches and usage scale turnovers for the player; for steals and blocks it is irrelevant, so should only be attached to the turnover form.

nba.opp_def_pos.reason: Allowed-by-position tables for turnovers and rim attempts blend scheme, pace and the individual opponent's role; noise dominates at the 1-3 count scale.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Blitz, zone and full-court pressure change gamble rates and so steals and deflections; drop coverage keeps the big at the rim and increases blocks; categorical labels need the player's role interaction.

nba.pace.reason: Possessions scale all events, but for blocks the relevant volume is opponent rim attempts and for steals opponent live-ball turnovers; pace is second-order.

nba.shot_profile.reason: Opponent rim attempts and rim share are the supply for blocks; stronger than pace and total FGA, and should be matched to the blocker's rim-protection minutes.

nba.scorer_bias.reason: Arena-level credit for steals and blocks has documented home-side tendencies; effect is modest but adds dispersion at 0.5-1.5 strikes; the size estimated by arena needs many seasons.

nba.garbage.reason: Minutes loss in blowouts matters; but steals can rise in garbage time when bench players press, so sign is role dependent; rebuild from ratings not the spread.

nba.foul_rates.reason: Aggressive shot-blockers pick up fouls and sit; the real link is the interaction with block attempts, not a standalone effect.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Availability of own rim anchors (who else blocks shots) and of the opponent's ball handlers changes event supply directly; vintage matters.

nba.stat_dist.reason: Overdispersed Poisson with minutes mixture is the right base, and for 0.5/1.5/2.5 strikes the dispersion matters more than the mean.

m.quote_history.reason: Price path is market state, not a driver of steals or blocks.

m.rules_text.reason: Rules fix that inactive players are voided at a fair price while entering players settle on actual counts; the stocks contract sums two categories.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook prop lines are benchmarks, not inputs; low-count lines are a favourite-longshot battleground.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Realised frequency by rung is calibration history; for these low-count events the rung hit-rates are the main reality check of dispersion.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: A Kalshi-specific overlay on probabilities, not an input to steals and blocks production.

m.volume_oi.reason: Open interest has no mechanism link to blocks or steals and mostly tracks popularity of the player.

m.trade_tape.reason: Order flow is market microstructure; no causal content for the count process.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Settled values are labels; for steals and blocks the official score sheet credit decisions make reconciliation necessary.

nba.stat_corrections.reason: Block and steal credits are among the most frequently revised box-score items after video review; matters for exact-threshold outcomes.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Intentional fouling affects free throws more than steals and blocks; minor effect here, retained only as context.

interactions.mechanism: Mean events equal rate times minutes, but rung probability at 2.5 or 3.5 is convex in the mean for a low-count process, so a small minutes increase raises the tail probability proportionally more than the mean; the effect is largest for a player whose mean sits near 1.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(count >= k) over minutes bins for fixed per-minute rate and compare with Poisson and negative binomial tails.

interactions.mechanism: A rim protector who contests aggressively both blocks more and fouls more, so the same behaviour that raises block supply raises foul-trouble risk and minute loss; this makes blocks and minutes negatively dependent in the tail.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate correlation between block count and minutes shortfall in games where the player had >=3 first-half fouls.

interactions.mechanism: A blitz or full-court scheme raises opponent live-ball turnovers only against careless handlers; against a low-turnover primary handler the extra pressure yields deflections without steals, so the effect of scheme on steals is conditional on the opponent handler's turnover rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact opponent handler turnover rate with scheme labels in a Poisson regression on team steals.

interactions.mechanism: Official-scorer credit adds dispersion that is large relative to a mean of 1-2 events, widening the count distribution and making the tail rungs likelier than a clean Poisson, with arena-specific shifts of a few percent of rate; the effect is strongest for steals and blocks, weak for rebounds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare dispersion indices of home-arena steal counts by arena over multiple seasons.

interactions.mechanism: The stocks sum has variance equal to the sum of variances plus twice the covariance; for versatile wings positive covariance raises the 4+ tail relative to independent components, while rim anchors have near-zero covariance.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare P(S+B >= 4) from independent components versus a copula by archetype against realised frequencies.

nonlinearities.shape: convex tail probability in the dispersion parameter
nonlinearities.why: At mean about 1 the probability of 3+ rises from roughly 8% to 12% when the negative-binomial dispersion index moves from 1.0 to 1.4, so rung probability is more sensitive to dispersion than to a 10% change in the mean.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating: shrinkage weight toward the role prior is large
nonlinearities.why: Per-minute rates for steals have a small signal-to-noise ratio across games, so predicted rates should pull strongly toward the role mean; the effective weight on a player's own rate is below 50% for a full season of data.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold at 3-4 fouls triggering benching
nonlinearities.why: For aggressive shot-blockers minutes fall sharply once fouls reach a coach's threshold, so the effect on blocks is a step in minutes rather than a smooth function of the foul rate.

contract.settlement_definition: No Kalshi series is filed under this archetype in the ledger, so nothing can be read. By blueprint the targets are Summer League game winner, spread and total, and tournament/season outcomes (league champion). Overtime format, tie handling, the number of minutes in a game, how a spread or total treats overtime, and the source of results are unverified; the neighbouring live series KXNBASUMMER (Summer League champion) and KXNBASUMMERPTS (Summer League player points) are filed under other archetypes and are TITLE_ONLY.
variants_and_edge_cases: Summer League formats differ from NBA regulation (shorter quarters at some events, a different overtime procedure, tournament with seeding and a final); whether Kalshi game totals include overtime and what happens to postponed games is unknown.
Multiple events exist (Las Vegas, California Classic, Utah) with different participating teams and formats; a contract's event identity changes the baseline parameters.
Tournament or 'Summer League champion' contracts depend on seeding rules (record, point differential tiebreak) as well as team strength, and consolation games lessen incentives.
Player-prop series for Summer League (KXNBASUMMERPTS) depend on rosters and minute plans announced game-day; their DNP and void rules are unverified.
contract.settlement_data_source: Unverified: Summer League official box scores (NBA.com) are the natural source but no rules text exists for this archetype.

mechanism.summary: Summer League outcomes are produced by rosters and decisions rather than by franchise strength: who actually plays (rookies, two-way and G League players, returning bench players), how long each plays under coach evaluation plans, how good those players are on a common scale given thin or non-NBA data, and a game environment (format, pace, defensive intensity) that differs from the regular season. The outcome distribution has large variance because rotations are fluid, defense and execution are loose, and teams sometimes prioritize evaluation over winning; incentives change with the tournament state. Information is scarce and arrives game-day through announcements rather than structured injury reports, which makes timing as important as level for any model.

stages.name: Roster and participation decisions
stages.description: The first stage is who is on the floor: drafted rookies, two-way players, returning bench players on contracts, G League invitees. A top pick may play one game then be shut down, and veterans sit once their evaluation is done. Announcements arrive game-day through informal channels and are the main information.
stages.distribution: Discrete participation states with team-policy-driven probabilities; high-impact players have a bimodal minutes distribution (full or zero).

stages.name: Coach minutes plans and rotations
stages.description: Coaches use Summer League to evaluate players, so minutes are allocated to give looks to all players rather than to maximize winning; rookies often have caps and second-round or two-way players receive extended minutes. Rotation patterns are less stable than in the regular season and are set by program philosophy.
stages.distribution: Plan-driven minute vectors with random deviations; minutes variance within player is high and cross-team variation is structural.

stages.name: Team strength from translated talent
stages.description: A team's Summer League strength is the minutes-weighted sum of players' strengths on a common scale. With limited NBA data for most participants, ratings must be translated from college, G League and international performance and drafted position, with large uncertainty and no cohesion effect from shared practice.
stages.distribution: Sum of independent uncertain player ratings; strength uncertainty large (sd of team rating of 5-8 points per 100 possessions) and heavy-tailed because of star presence.

stages.name: Game environment: format, pace and variance
stages.description: The format (period length, overtime rules, foul limits) and talent mix produce a different scoring environment: more possessions per minute, weaker half-court defense and larger point-total variance. League-specific baselines are required, and event-level differences exist between sites.
stages.distribution: Margin and total distributions with larger sd than the regular season (margin sd about 14-16 per 40-48 minutes, to be estimated); tie and overtime probabilities depend on format.

stages.name: Incentive state and schedule
stages.description: The tournament structure gives some games importance (seeding for the final) while others are for evaluation only, and schedule density in a short event affects rest decisions. The effect is on minutes and effort and varies across the week.
stages.distribution: State-dependent: effort and bench depth shift discretely between meaningful and meaningless games.

talent_strength.note: Translated player strength for those without NBA ratings.

opponent_matchup.note: With rosters assembled days before and few repeated opponents, matchup-specific scheme effects are not identifiable from Summer League history and add little beyond team strength and pace.

role_personnel.note: Minutes plans and who plays; the dominant signal.

nba.sl_talent_translation.label: Talent translation of rookies, two-way and G League players to a common Summer League strength scale
nba.sl_talent_translation.mechanism: Most Summer League minutes go to players without NBA data, so team strength must come from translating college, international and G League performance to an equivalent NBA-level rating.
nba.sl_talent_translation.rationale: A franchise's NBA rating says little about its Summer League roster; the strength is the minutes-weighted sum of translated player ratings, and uncertainty is large because translation factors are noisy.
nba.sl_talent_translation.measurement: For each player build a prior rating from available sources: college BPM/box-score composite (translation coefficient estimated historically by regressing NBA first-year BPM on college BPM with age and pace adjustments), G League per-minute production translated by a league-quality factor (about 0.6-0.7 estimated by backtest), international league adjustments; shrink to draft-slot prior (pick position mean) with prior weight 15 games-equivalent; team rating = minutes-weighted sum with expected minutes from announced rosters. As-of: roster announcement time.
raw_data: college and G League per-minute statistics, draft slot, age
nba.sl_talent_translation.why: Replaces the unavailable NBA impact rating with a measurable prior for the players who actually play.

nba.sl_minutes_plan_hazard.label: Probability that a drafted player or returning rotation player plays, sits or is shut down
nba.sl_minutes_plan_hazard.mechanism: Summer League teams manage minutes for prospects and shut down players after a few games or when they are established; the probability a top prospect plays in a given game is a decision, not an injury process.
nba.sl_minutes_plan_hazard.rationale: The minutes a star rookie plays varies from full to zero by team policy, game number and announcements; the market impact is large because a top pick may account for a big share of team scoring.
nba.sl_minutes_plan_hazard.measurement: From past Summer Leagues build a table by draft slot (1-5, 6-14, 15-30, second round), years of experience and game number of the share of games played and minutes distribution; compute shutdown hazards after game k given previous game minutes (logistic); combine with announced status via a calibrated map from announcement language (will play, game-time, shut down) to realised participation. As-of: last announcement before the order time.
free_sources: Beat-writer announcements (X/Twitter, team websites), SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for archival access
raw_data: historical SL box scores with minutes by player; announcement text with timestamps
nba.sl_minutes_plan_hazard.why: Gives the structural distribution for the single largest Summer League uncertainty, whether the best player plays.

nba.sl_game_importance_incentive.label: Game importance and incentive state (tournament seeding, championship eligibility, evaluation goals)
nba.sl_game_importance_incentive.mechanism: Teams in Summer League care about evaluation and sometimes about the tournament; their minutes and effort depend on whether the game matters for seeding or the final.
nba.sl_game_importance_incentive.rationale: Win-maximizing effort is not the default: after a team is eliminated or clinched it plays deeper bench and evaluation lineups, which changes both the winner and the totals; the effect is predictable from the standings state.
nba.sl_game_importance_incentive.measurement: Compute for each team and game an indicator of seeding relevance (probability the game changes championship qualification based on standings and tiebreaks, evaluated from remaining schedule) and the team's historical bench-depth shift when eliminated; features: P(game matters), games played so far, whether prior game was a back-to-back. As-of: after the previous game's result.
free_sources: NBA.com Summer League standings and format pages
raw_data: standings and tournament rules by year, schedule
nba.sl_game_importance_incentive.why: Captures effort/rotation incentives that vary within the Summer League week and have no analog in the regular season.

nba.sl_format_scoring_baseline.label: Summer League-specific scoring, pace and margin variance baseline by format
nba.sl_format_scoring_baseline.mechanism: Summer League has a different game format (quarter length, overtime rule, fouling rules) and talent level, so scoring totals, pace and margin variance differ from the regular season and must be estimated from Summer League games.
nba.sl_format_scoring_baseline.rationale: Applying regular-season totals and margin sd to Summer League misstates both: games are typically higher scoring per possession with weaker defense and higher variance, so spread and total probabilities need league-specific parameters.
nba.sl_format_scoring_baseline.measurement: From all Summer League games over the last 5 events compute mean total, standard deviation of total and margin, tie-at-regulation frequency, OT frequency, and pace in possessions per 40 or 48 minutes depending on format; model margin as normal with sd by league (Las Vegas, California Classic, Salt Lake City) and shrink event-level sd to the pooled value (prior weight 30 games); update with games already played in the current event. As-of: games before tip.
free_sources: nba_api summer league (leagueid 15), SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for coverage
raw_data: game results, period scores, possessions, event identifiers
nba.sl_format_scoring_baseline.why: Provides correct variance and totals scale for spread and total contracts in a league with little history.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Back-to-back and short-turnaround schedule density in Las Vegas affects rest decisions for prospects; secondary to the minutes plan itself.

nba.news.reason: Roster announcements, shutdown decisions and rest news arrive game-day and shift the strength estimate most; correct primary variable but the existing label lumps it with trades and coaching news.

nba.rotation.reason: Coach minutes plans (equal-time evaluation, rookie caps) override win-maximizing rotations; the structure differs from the regular season and history is thin.

interactions.mechanism: Team strength is the minutes-weighted sum of player ratings, so the same rating matters more for a player with 28 expected minutes than one with 10; a top pick who is shut down removes both his rating and the minutes, producing a step in team strength rather than a gradual change.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare team margin with and without the top-drafted player across past Summer Leagues, controlling for opponent.

interactions.mechanism: Summer League totals are both higher-variance and higher-pace than regular-season; the variance of totals scales with possessions and with defensive looseness, so the sd of total and sd of margin move together with the format baseline.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate total and margin sd by event and format from past Summer League results and test heteroskedasticity versus pace.

interactions.mechanism: A late announcement that a key rookie rests switches the team to a different regime (bench-heavy rotation, evaluation lineups); the market reaction depends on timing, and the same news before and after the order time has different value.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the move in team margin conditional on announcement timestamps relative to the prior price time.

interactions.mechanism: Importance and schedule density jointly determine who rests: on the second game of a back-to-back with no seeding stakes, minutes shift to bench and prospects, whereas the same schedule in a must-win game keeps starters; the effect of rest depends on stakes.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress minutes of top prospects on back-to-back x importance indicator across past events.

nonlinearities.shape: bimodal/step: top prospects play full or not at all
nonlinearities.why: The impact of a top pick on team strength is not proportional to expected minutes because the distribution is bimodal; mean-minutes models understate the variance of team strength and the effect of announcements.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy-tailed star effect: team strength is dominated by one or two high-talent players
nonlinearities.why: Summer League rosters contain few players above NBA-rotation level and their share of usage is large, so team strength is convex in the top player's rating.

nonlinearities.shape: heteroskedastic: margin sd larger in blowout-prone mismatches and in loose-defense formats
nonlinearities.why: Summer League games have higher variance than regular-season games and variance grows with talent gaps, so normal approximations with a fixed sd misprice tails.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNBATEAMTOTAL is a binary over/under on one named team's points in the named game: YES if the team scores more than the half-point strike (floor_strike 135.5, strike_type greater, so no push). A game postponed but starting within 48 hours stays open and resolves on the official final result; a game cancelled or not started within 48 hours resolves all markets at a fair price. The sampled rules do not say whether overtime points count, so the OT inclusion that the existing draft asserts is not verified; the ledger has only one series for this archetype.

rules_evidence.quote: If Oklahoma City scores more than 135.5 points in the Oklahoma City vs Memphis Pro Basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 6, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Strike construction: 'more than X.5' on one team's points in the whole game, so no push and a single-team count.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start time, the market will remain open and resolve based on the official final result.
rules_evidence.establishes: Postponement within 48 hours keeps the market open and uses the official final result.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is cancelled or not started within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start, all markets will resolve to a fair price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Cancellation or long delay voids at a fair price, not NO.

variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime: the sampled primary and secondary text never mention overtime; 'the official final result' of a game normally includes OT points, which would add roughly 11-13 points to each team in about 6% of games, but this is unverified and changes tail probabilities.

Strike construction: the sampled strike of 135.5 for Oklahoma City is well above a typical team total (about 115-120), consistent with a ladder of rungs; the contract is a single threshold per market with no push at half-point strikes.

Team total is not a function of a single team's offense: it depends on the shared possession count and the opponent's play, so correlated markets (game total, spread, opponent team total) must be internally consistent.
Void on cancellation or a delay beyond 48 hours pays a fair price, so late-season games affected by weather or travel have no NO risk but no information either.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final score of the game as published by the league; the sampled rules refer to 'the official final result' without naming a provider.

mechanism.summary: A team's points equal the shared number of possessions times its points per possession, plus overtime if counted. Possessions are a joint property of both teams (the slower style tends to dominate), while points per possession come from the matchup of own offense with the opponent's defense decomposed into shooting, turnovers, offensive rebounds and free throws, with tonight's availability changing every factor. Game script then bends the result: a favorite's points flatten in garbage time, an underdog's rise from late fouling and deep-bench scoring, so team points are a nonlinear function of expected margin. Variance depends on style (three-point reliance, pace) and is large relative to strike spacing, and the settlement wording on overtime determines whether a 6% mixture component of about a dozen points is part of the distribution.

stages.name: Shared possessions
stages.description: The game's possession count is one number determined jointly by both teams' tempo preferences, transition rates and turnovers; averaging the two teams' season paces misstates it, since the slower style tends to dominate. Lineup changes (a missing point guard) shift tempo for the whole game.
stages.distribution: Roughly normal with mean near 98-100 and sd 4-5 possessions; a right skew from OT; correlated with both teams' scoring.

stages.name: Own offense against the opponent's defense
stages.description: Points per possession depend on own shot quality, turnover and offensive rebound tendencies, free throws and the opponent's defensive profile in each factor. The additive offensive-minus-defensive rating approximates this but the factor decomposition handles scheme-specific deviations such as a rim-heavy offense against a drop defense.
stages.distribution: Efficiency per 100 possessions with sd across teams of about 4; matchup deviations of 1-2 points; per-game noise dominated by three-point variance.

stages.name: Availability and unit changes
stages.description: Absence of own scorers lowers offensive rating and also changes pace; absence of the opponent's rim protector or point-of-attack defender raises it. Starters are confirmed shortly before tip and rotation changes alter the expected minutes of the best units.
stages.distribution: Discrete personnel states with rating shifts of 1-5 points per 100 possessions per key absence.

stages.name: Shooting variance and free throws
stages.description: Single-game three-point shooting luck of both teams, and the foul-and-free-throw environment (crew tendencies, bonus), are the largest random components of points; they regress to expectation between games and have style-dependent variance. Free throws contribute 3-4 points per game across crews.
stages.distribution: Team points sd about 11-14, larger for three-point-reliant teams; shooting shocks are positively correlated between the two teams' totals through pace.

stages.name: Game script and overtime
stages.description: Win probability bends team points: favorites' starters sit in garbage time, underdogs score late through fouling and bench possessions; the mapping from expected margin to team points is nonlinear. Overtime, if counted, adds a mixture component of about a dozen points with probability near 6%.
stages.distribution: Skewed conditional distribution; mixture with an OT component whose size is about 11-13 points and weight about 5-7%.

stages.name: Settlement
stages.description: Settlement is the official final score for the named team above a half-point strike; cancellation and long delays void at a fair price. The sampled rules do not say whether overtime counts, which is the largest unknown.
stages.distribution: Binary indicator on integer points; no push.

nba.four_factors_matchup.label: Expected four factors for own offense vs opponent defense (eFG%, turnover rate, offensive rebound rate, free-throw rate)
nba.four_factors_matchup.mechanism: Team points per possession decompose into shooting efficiency, turnovers, offensive rebounds and free-throw rate; each factor responds to the specific opponent differently than the overall rating does.
nba.four_factors_matchup.rationale: Offensive rating against defensive rating is an additive approximation; a rim-heavy offense against a drop defense, or a turnover-prone offense against a pressure defense, deviates from it, and the factor-level decomposition allows shot profile, scheme and luck to enter in the right place.
nba.four_factors_matchup.measurement: For each team compute offensive and defensive four factors per 100 possessions over last 25 games (half-life 12) and season, opponent-adjusted by the standard iterative method; expected eFG = league + (own offense - league) + (opp defense allowed - league) with team-specific shrinkage weights (prior weight 20 games); combine factors into expected points per 100 using regression weights (eFG about 0.4, TOV 0.25, ORB 0.2, FT 0.15). As-of: games before tip, with lineup adjustments for absentees.
raw_data: team game box scores: FGM, FG3M, FGA, TOV, OREB, FTA, possessions
nba.four_factors_matchup.why: Allows each of shot-quality, turnover pressure and free-throw rate to differ by opponent; matches the contract's single-team scoring.

nba.joint_pace_interaction.label: Joint matchup pace from both teams' pace preferences (slower-team weight and transition vs half-court)
nba.joint_pace_interaction.mechanism: Game possessions are one shared number whose expectation is not the average of two teams' paces; the slower style tends to dominate and transition-heavy teams are constrained by opponent turnovers and rebounds.
nba.joint_pace_interaction.rationale: A team's total depends on the shared possession count, so error in the pace of the matchup translates directly into points; averaging season paces misstates a matchup of a fast team vs a slow team.
nba.joint_pace_interaction.measurement: From 5 seasons of games regress game possessions on both teams' season paces (adjusted for home), their interaction and style flags (transition share, post-up share) to get weights (e.g. 0.55 on the slower team); add lineup adjustment from projected starters; residual sd by matchup type (fast-fast, fast-slow). Output expected possessions and sd. As-of: tip.
raw_data: team-game possessions, pace, play-type frequencies
nba.joint_pace_interaction.why: Gives the correct possession count for the matchup rather than a single-team pace.

nba.team_points_variance_by_style.label: Style-dependent variance of a team's points (three-point reliance, transition share, pace)
nba.team_points_variance_by_style.mechanism: Teams that take many threes and play fast have higher game-to-game variance in points than slow half-court teams; the over/under probability at a given strike depends on the sd, not only the mean.
nba.team_points_variance_by_style.rationale: A team total strike near the mean has probability near 50% regardless of variance, but strikes at 5-10 points away depend on the sd; the sd is team- and matchup-specific and is typically 11-14 points.
nba.team_points_variance_by_style.measurement: Compute each team's residual sd of points (actual minus rating-based expectation, no market lines) over a season with regression on three-point attempt rate, pace and opponent style; shrink to league sd (about 12.5) with prior weight 25 games; combine own sd and opponent style effects; model the points distribution as skew-normal with skew from blowout probability. As-of: games before tip.
raw_data: team-game points, 3PA rate, pace
nba.team_points_variance_by_style.why: Provides the shape parameter needed to price strikes away from the mean and the asymmetry of tails.

nba.team_points_margin_curve.label: Expected team points as a function of the game's expected margin (winner-loser asymmetry and garbage-time shape)
nba.team_points_margin_curve.mechanism: A team's points are not linear in the expected margin: favorites' points flatten (garbage time) and underdogs gain late points through fouling and deep-bench scoring, so the mapping from win probability to team points is a curve.
nba.team_points_margin_curve.rationale: Deriving team totals as (total ± spread)/2 assumes linearity; the empirical curve can differ by 1-2 points at large spreads, and this matters for strikes in a market keyed to the team's own points.
nba.team_points_margin_curve.measurement: From 5 seasons of games compute realised team points minus rating-based expected points as a function of pregame expected margin built from ratings (not the spread) in bins of 2 points; fit a monotone-spline of own points on expected margin with total environment as a covariate; use leave-one-season-out cross-validation; output expected team points given expected margin and total.
free_sources: Computed from nba_api game logs and team ratings
raw_data: team-game points, pregame expected margin from ratings
nba.team_points_margin_curve.why: Replaces the benchmark-derived implied team total with a market-free curve.

nba.def_rtg.reason: Opponent defense enters through points allowed per possession; defensive ratings are noisier than offensive ones and their interaction with the offense's shot profile is not additive.

nba.pace.reason: Possessions are a joint property of both teams; the label says 'own possessions', which misstates the mechanism: only the game's shared possession count exists, and the slower team's style tends to dominate.

nba.implied_team_totals.reason: Derived from the sportsbook spread and total; it is the market's price for this very contract, so labelled primary it would make a model equal to the market; keep only for the consistency check.

nba.lineup_adj_rating.reason: Tonight's active set changes offense by several points per 100; essential, but 'availability-adjusted offense' needs lineup-specific offense/defense separation rather than a single net rating.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Own scorers and opponent rim protectors both move expected points; vintage matters because starters are confirmed shortly before tip.

nba.usage.reason: Usage redistribution among own players changes who scores but barely changes team points; the existing text says as much, so this belongs as context for player markets rather than a team-total driver.

nba.shot_profile.reason: Own shot mix against the opponent's allowed mix sets expected efficiency; stable and the basis for the four-factors expectation.

nba.three_pt_luck.reason: Own and opponent 3P% regression matters for forecasting team points from recent results; effect modest per game but the main reason recent point totals mislead.

nba.fouls_ft.reason: Free-throw rate and crew foul tendency change points from the line (about 3-4 points per game across crews); must be combined with game script because trailing teams foul more.

nba.garbage.reason: Garbage time lowers the favorite's points while the underdog scores against bench units and via late fouls; sign differs by team, so this is the key skew input; rebuilt from ratings, not the spread.

nba.ot_model.reason: OT adds roughly 11-13 points for a team in about 6% of games; relevant only if OT counts, which the sampled rules do not state.

interactions.mechanism: Own efficiency against this defense depends on factor-level fit: a rim-heavy offense gains against a drop defense that concedes rim attempts, but loses against one that walls the paint; the additive rating difference averages these opposite cases and so errs systematically for extreme styles.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare error of additive rating prediction versus the four-factor matchup prediction for teams in the top and bottom rim-rate quintiles.

interactions.mechanism: The favorite's expected points flatten when the game becomes lopsided because starters sit while the underdog's points keep rising through late fouls and bench scoring; the relation of team points to margin is piecewise with a kink around a 10-12 point expected margin.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit a spline of own points on expected margin using ratings and check for the kink separately for favorites and underdogs.

interactions.mechanism: A missing ball handler lowers both team efficiency and the possession count; the two effects multiply in the points total so a model that adjusts only the rating understates the points drop, and the opponent's points move too through the shared pace.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare team points and possessions in games without the primary handler versus with, controlling for opponent.

interactions.mechanism: Trailing teams foul late and the leading team shoots the free throws, so crew foul tendency raises the favorite's points more in close games and the underdog's points via fouls drawn in garbage time; effect depends on the margin path.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate FT points by team and margin bin, interacted with crew foul rate.

interactions.mechanism: A three-point-reliant team has high variance in points, so strikes far from the mean have probability much different from a low-variance team; luck regression (the three-point mean) and variance (the dispersion) are separate parameters that both matter for strike distance.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare calibration of P(over) at strikes 6+ points from the mean using team-specific versus pooled variance.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold with asymmetric effect on favorite and underdog
nonlinearities.why: Beyond about a 15-point margin late, starters sit and the favorite's points fall, while the underdog's points rise slightly; the relation is not monotone in blowout probability and differs by side.

nonlinearities.shape: mixture step: about 6% probability of adding roughly a dozen points if OT counts
nonlinearities.why: The team-points distribution acquires a right-hand lump from OT; the over probability for high strikes is lifted by the mixture while the central probability is nearly unaffected.

nonlinearities.shape: concave in possession count for points: efficiency declines as pace increases
nonlinearities.why: Faster pace raises possessions but lowers per-possession efficiency slightly (quicker shots), so points rise less than proportionally with pace.

contract.settlement_definition: Eleven unregistered series settle on season-long or event-level outcomes for 2026-27: division winners (best regular-season record in the division, ties by the league's official tiebreak rules), highest-scoring performance (YES if the named player scores at least the threshold in any regular-season game, overtime included), player stat average (YES if the player's per-game average, as the rounded figure from the source agencies, is at least the strike; zero games played is an average of zero and league qualification minimums do not apply), longest win streak (any team with a regular-season streak of at least N games), last undefeated team (the team whose first loss comes latest by day, ties splitting $1/N) and the Cup Finals matchup (resolves immediately upon qualification of the two teams). Only regular season games count for the streak, undefeated, high-score and average series, with Cup games before the Championship game counted.
