rules_evidence.establishes: Single-game threshold in any regular-season game, overtime points count.

rules_evidence.quote: Player averages are based on the rounded figure as reported by the Source Agencies.
rules_evidence.establishes: Average contracts resolve on the rounded published figure, not the unrounded ratio.

rules_evidence.quote: If Zach LaVine does not play in any games in the 2026-27 Pro Basketball regular season, then he is deemed to have averaged zero three-pointers made per game.
rules_evidence.establishes: A player with zero games played has an average of zero, so availability enters the outcome only through games actually played.

rules_evidence.quote: NBA Cup games before the Championship game are part of the regular season and do count towards a winning streak.
rules_evidence.establishes: Cup group and knockout games count towards streaks; the final and playoffs do not.

rules_evidence.quote: measured by the day of their first loss (not exact time)
rules_evidence.establishes: Last undefeated is determined by calendar day of first loss, so same-day losses are ties paying 1/N.

rules_evidence.quote: If teams are tied for the best record within the division, the winner is determined using the governing league's official tie-breaking rules.
rules_evidence.establishes: Division ties are broken by the official hierarchy rather than split.

rules_evidence.quote: Resolution occurs immediately upon qualification, not when the game is actually played.
rules_evidence.establishes: Cup Finals matchup resolves when the two teams qualify, so the event is bracket progression, not the Finals game.

variants_and_edge_cases: Average contracts (KXNBASTATAVG) use the rounded published figure with no league minimum qualification: a player who plays only a few games can still qualify on a small sample, and a player who plays none averages zero.

Highest-scoring performance counts overtime points in any regular-season game; if the player already met the threshold the contract is determined, and the remaining-games probability only matters for the not-yet-achieved case.
Win-streak and last-undefeated series count regular-season games including Cup games but not the Cup final or the play-in; last-undefeated is by day with ties paying $1/N rounded down.

Division and Cup matchup contracts depend on tiebreak rules and bracket structure respectively, not on a stat; the existing catalog entry (triple doubles and combos) does not describe any of the live series.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league statistics and standings via the 'Source Agencies' named in the full rules; the sampled text refers to them without naming them, so the specific agencies and how late corrections are handled are unverified.

mechanism.summary: The live series in this unregistered bucket are a collection of long-horizon functionals rather than single-game milestones. A season three-point average is attempts per game times make probability, observed over games actually played, with a published rounded threshold. A highest-scoring game is the maximum of a heavy-tailed scoring distribution over the games a player plays, driven by minutes, usage, hot shooting, free throws and overtime. Division winners, win streaks of 20 and the last undefeated team are functionals of a team simulation: game win probabilities with strength uncertainty and star availability, aggregated into records with tiebreaks, run lengths and first-loss dates. The Cup Finals matchup is the product of two single-elimination bracket outcomes resolved at qualification. The existing draft's DD-oriented mechanism does not apply to these; the common elements are availability over the season and the rule-specific aggregation.

stages.name: Season availability and games played
stages.description: Everything long-horizon depends on how many games the relevant players play and how healthy stars are: a three-point average only counts games played, the maximum only runs over games played, and team contracts depend on star availability. Load management, injuries and trades define the games-played distribution.
stages.distribution: Mixture with most mass at 60-78 games and a long left tail; zero games is a possible outcome that settles the average at zero.

stages.name: Per-game rate for an average contract
stages.description: A season three-point average is attempts per game times make probability. Attempts depend on role and teammates and are persistent; make probability is mostly luck regressing strongly toward talent in a season-long window. Early-season shooting should be shrunk, and the rounded published figure sets the effective threshold.
stages.distribution: Average of games with variance falling as sd/sqrt(n); posterior of true rate is approximately Gaussian with sd 0.1-0.3 threes per game early in the season.

stages.name: Single-game scoring tail
stages.description: Reaching 54 requires an extreme combination of high minutes, usage, shooting luck, free throws and often overtime; the per-game probability is on the order of tenths of a percent for the best scorers, and the probability over the season compounds across remaining games. Blowouts cut it, overtime raises it.
stages.distribution: Heavy right tail (generalised Pareto beyond about 35 points); per-game exceedance 0.1-1% for elite scorers; compound over games played.

stages.name: Team simulation for division, streak and undefeated contracts
stages.description: Game win probabilities from ratings and rest, with strength uncertainty and star availability, aggregate into division records with tiebreaks, runs of consecutive wins across 30 teams, and the first-loss date for each unbeaten team. Dependence arises from shared opponents and from head-to-head games.
stages.distribution: Poisson-binomial records; run-length (Markov chain) distribution for streaks; first-passage distribution of first loss with day-level ties.

stages.name: Cup bracket and matchup resolution
stages.description: The Finals matchup depends on group qualification and the bracket's single-elimination games on neutral courts; the contract resolves upon qualification of the two teams. The probability of a given pair is a product of two bracket-outcome probabilities (if the brackets are conference based).
stages.distribution: Single-elimination bracket outcomes with per-game win probabilities near rating-implied values; product structure across brackets.

stages.name: Settlement forms
stages.description: Settlement details determine the functional: rounding for the average, overtime inclusion for the maximum, counting of Cup games for streaks, calendar-day ties for last undefeated, tiebreak hierarchy for divisions and qualification timing for the matchup. Each is read from the series rules.
stages.distribution: Deterministic aggregation rules applied to the simulated outcomes; ties split $1/N where stated.

talent_strength.note: Player scoring/shooting talent for the individual contracts and team strength for the team simulations.

opponent_matchup.note: Season-long averages, a maximum over games and team-level streaks are dominated by availability and rating; opponent-specific matchup effects average out and are not worth a separate input for these contracts.

role_personnel.note: Role and minutes drive attempts and ceiling games; in teams the lineup is captured by availability.

availability_news.note: Season-level availability is the dominant uncertainty.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach changes in role, minutes and rest policy (and star load management) affect games played and usage across a season but no input quantifies them for these contracts.

environment.note: Neither a season average nor a division race depends on venue-specific features beyond what ratings and schedule capture; single-game ceiling is only weakly affected by arena.

game_context_script.note: Blowout and overtime context for the maximum; bracket progression for the matchup.

pace_volume.note: Attempt volume per game and team pace for scoring ceilings.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shooting luck regression for the average and hot-game tail for the maximum.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and clinching incentives and division race state; load management is only implied.

officiating_rules.note: Tiebreak hierarchy and Cup bracket rules as the governing rule set; referee behaviour irrelevant.

settlement_contract.note: Rounded average, zero games, OT inclusion, day-level ties and qualification resolution.

nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.label: Per-game tail model for a player's maximum single-game points (exceedance of 50+/54+ and overtime contribution)
nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.mechanism: A highest-scoring-performance contract is the maximum over about 70 games of a heavy-tailed scoring distribution, with extreme nights requiring high minutes, hot shooting, free throws and often overtime.
nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.rationale: The mean scoring rate is nearly irrelevant for 54+; the exceedance probability per game is a tail quantity that must be estimated with a peaks-over-threshold model and then compounded over remaining games (1 - (1-p)^G).
nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.measurement: For each candidate fit a generalised Pareto to the exceedances of points over 35 in games with minutes >= 32 over 3 seasons, with league-wide shape shrinkage (prior weight 40 exceedances) and player-specific scale; estimate per-game P(pts >= 54) = P(game >= 35) x GPD tail beyond 54, adding an OT adjustment (OT games contribute about 6% and add about 6-8 points for stars); then P(at least one in remaining G games) = 1 - E[(1 - p)^G] with games-played uncertainty. Also track the season-to-date maximum (already achieved events resolve YES if the strike was met).
raw_data: player-game points, minutes, OT flag, season-to-date maximum
nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.why: Prices KXNBAPLAYERHIGHSCORE directly; the existing milestone-rate input addresses a different event.

nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.label: Season-average state with rounding rule: unrounded to rounded threshold and remaining games
nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.mechanism: The contract uses the rounded per-game figure from the source agencies, so the effective threshold on the unrounded average is half a rounding unit below the stated strike, and the average itself converges as games accumulate.
nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.rationale: A 2.6+ three-pointers per game contract resolves on the rounded value, so a true average of 2.55 counts as 2.6 (at one-decimal rounding); ignoring the rounding shifts the threshold and its uncertainty is smaller as the season progresses; zero games played counts as an average of zero.
nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.measurement: State = (makes to date, games played, games remaining); posterior of the player's rest-of-season average (shrunk) times remaining games plus makes to date gives the final average distribution; compute P(round(final_avg, 1) >= strike) = P(final_avg >= strike - 0.05) (verify the exact rounding rule), include the probability of playing zero games (settles at 0) and the denominator being games actually played. As-of: nightly after games.
raw_data: player-game makes, games played, remaining team schedule
nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.why: Gives the exact functional form of the average-threshold contract, including the rounding and zero-games rule.

nba.team_win_streak_hazard.label: Hazard of a team reaching a 20-game winning streak (run-length chain with heterogeneous game win probabilities)
nba.team_win_streak_hazard.mechanism: A 20-game win streak requires 20 consecutive wins; with game win probabilities of 75-85% for the best team, the chance depends on the full sequence of probabilities, their correlation through star health and schedule, and the number of teams that could qualify.
nba.team_win_streak_hazard.rationale: Averaging a team's win probability underestimates the chance because a streak concentrates in stretches of weak opponents and healthy rosters; the league-wide market is a union over 30 teams and about 60 windows each.
nba.team_win_streak_hazard.measurement: For each team and each window of 20 consecutive scheduled games compute the product of game win probabilities from ratings and rest (with a star-health scenario mixture); P(streak >= 20 for team i) = 1 - prod over windows via a Markov chain with state = current run length; combine across teams assuming approximate independence except head-to-head links; include Cup games (they count) and exclude the Cup final and playoffs. As-of: nightly; update current runs.
raw_data: schedule with opponents and dates, ratings, current run length per team
nba.team_win_streak_hazard.why: Provides the structure for KXNBAWINSTREAK (20+), where the union over many teams and windows matters.

nba.undefeated_start_survival.label: Survival probability of undefeated starts by calendar day (last remaining unbeaten team)
nba.undefeated_start_survival.mechanism: The last undefeated team is the one whose first loss comes latest, measured by the date of the first loss, so the market depends on survival functions of each team and ties by date.
nba.undefeated_start_survival.rationale: The product of win probabilities gives each team's survival, but the contract resolves by the day of the first loss and splits ties when several teams lose on the same day, so the probability of a team being last depends on ties and calendar clustering.
nba.undefeated_start_survival.measurement: For each team compute S_i(d) = product over games on days <= d of P(win) (from ratings, rest and home/away); P(team i is the last undefeated) = sum over days of P(i's first loss on day d and all others have lost by day d), with ties on the same day sharing 1/N; compute by simulation with dependence from shared opponents. As-of: nightly; early in the season (about 8-10 games played) the field is nearly resolved.
raw_data: schedule with dates, ratings, current records
nba.undefeated_start_survival.why: Directly captures the date-based tie rule of KXNBALASTTOLOSE.

nba.division_race_tiebreak_state.label: Division-race state: records, remaining division games and tiebreak ledger
nba.division_race_tiebreak_state.mechanism: Division winner contracts are decided by the best record in a five-team division with the league's tiebreak procedure; division head-to-head games and divisional records feed the tiebreak.
nba.division_race_tiebreak_state.rationale: Division races are narrower than conference races; a tie occurs in about 10% of divisions and division records are the first tiebreaker after head-to-head, so the state of divisional games matters more than overall strength.
nba.division_race_tiebreak_state.measurement: For each division compute records, remaining intra-division games, head-to-head ledger and division record to date; simulate remaining season with team-strength uncertainty and apply the official tiebreak order for ties; output P(division winner) with tie contributions; update nightly. As-of: after each game.
raw_data: standings, schedule, head-to-head results
nba.division_race_tiebreak_state.why: Needed for the six division-winner series in this archetype.

nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.label: Probability of a specific Cup Finals pairing as the product of two conference bracket outcomes
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.mechanism: The Cup Finals pair is formed by the two semifinal winners (one from each conference bracket, if the bracket is conference-based), so the pair probability is a product of two independent single-elimination outcomes.
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.rationale: The matchup contract resolves immediately upon qualification, not when the game is played; its probability depends on group results, quarterfinal and semifinal match-ups and neutral-site single-game probabilities.
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.measurement: Compute P(team A reaches final) from group-stage results (qualifier probability), quarterfinal bracket draw and single-game win probabilities (neutral-site, with rest) and similarly for team B in the other bracket; P(pair) = P(A reaches final) x P(B reaches final) under independence across conference brackets (verify bracket structure from rules). As-of: nightly during the Cup.
raw_data: Cup standings, bracket, ratings
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.why: Gives the product structure and timing rule for KXNBAMATCHUP.

nba.milestone_rates.reason: Built for single-game double and triple doubles, yet none of the 11 live series is a triple double or combo ladder; only the highest-scoring-performance series resembles a single-game threshold, and for that the relevant base rate is points tail exceedance, not DD frequency.

nba.stat_dist.reason: Distribution of single-game points and made threes is the core of the highest-score and per-game-average series; the tail of points is what the 54+ contract prices and the sd of threes sets the variance of a season average.

nba.combo_covariance.reason: Covariance among points, rebounds and assists is irrelevant to the live contracts (division winners, a points high, a three-point average, win streaks, last undefeated, Cup final matchup); kept from a draft written for combo ladders that are not in the ledger.

nba.minutes.reason: Minutes per game drives both a season three-point average and the chance of a 54+ game (which needs a very high-minutes game, often with overtime).

nba.usage.reason: Usage determines attempts for scoring spikes and the volume for a three-point average; for the team contracts it is irrelevant.

nba.pace.reason: Pace of the opponent and of the team scales per-game attempts and thus both the average and the single-game ceiling; second-order.

nba.garbage.reason: Blowouts cut stars' minutes and so reduce 54+ chances while close games and overtime raise them; matter for the single-game series only.

nba.opp_def_pos.reason: Positional allowances are too noisy at the single-game extreme and irrelevant to the team contracts; the weak signal is dominated by the player's own tail.

nba.three_volume.reason: 3PA per game and make rate determine the 2.6 threes per game average in KXNBASTATAVG; shrinkage of make rate is needed, and the label's four bundled quantities should be split.

nba.player_shooting_regression.reason: A season average of threes made is the product of attempts and make rate; early-season hot or cold shooting must be regressed since the contract is season-long.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Games played over the full season is the dominant uncertainty for an average and for the single-game maximum; and star availability determines division and streak outcomes; needs time-resolved version.

nba.rotation.reason: Rotation patterns affect minutes within games, but none of the live series depends on lineup-level rotation at a granularity that this input supplies.

interactions.mechanism: Shrinkage of an early make-rate outlier depends on attempts to date and on the closeness of the rounded threshold: a player whose projected average sits within 0.05 of the strike is highly sensitive to the shrinkage constant, while one far from it is not, so the effective information value of regression depends on distance to the rounding boundary.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(avg >= strike) under different shrinkage constants as a function of the distance of the projected average to the strike.

interactions.mechanism: A 54-point night needs about 38 or more minutes, which arises mainly in close games and overtime; the probability of a ceiling game therefore jumps for games with high closeness probability and is negligible when blowout probability is high, a threshold-like dependence on game closeness.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate exceedance frequency of 45+ points by closeness bin and OT indicator for high-usage scorers.

interactions.mechanism: A star's absence switches a team from a high-win-probability regime to a lower one, and a 20-game streak requires the healthy regime in all games; the chance of the union over windows is therefore dominated by scenarios where stars are healthy throughout.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare streak probability from a star-health mixture versus a fixed average rating using historical long streaks.

interactions.mechanism: Early-season survival and division-race outcomes are linked through the same game results and schedule overlaps; an early loss for a division leader both ends the undefeated streak and shifts the division odds, so these contracts are positively dependent through team strength.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate both with common random numbers and check the correlation of the events for the same team.

interactions.mechanism: The pair probability is a product of two bracket outcomes whose probabilities are each a product of per-game neutral-site win probabilities; small per-game edges compound multiplicatively across three games, and rest differences before single elimination can shift each factor.
interactions.how_to_test: Back-test the product structure on previous Cup brackets and compare to realised pair frequencies.

nonlinearities.shape: step at the rounding boundary and convergence in games played
nonlinearities.why: The rounded average creates a step at strike minus half a unit; the distribution of the final average tightens with games played, so probability is a sigmoid whose slope rises as the season progresses.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy-tailed (generalised Pareto) with compounding over games
nonlinearities.why: Per-game exceedance of 54 is tenths of a percent but compounds over about 70 games, so the season probability is 1 - (1-p)^G and is very sensitive to the tail shape parameter.

nonlinearities.shape: multiplicative decay in run length: probability of 20 in a row is a product of 20 factors
nonlinearities.why: At a 80% per-game win probability the chance of 20 consecutive wins is about 1%; at 85% it is about 4%, so tiny rating differences produce large streak probability differences.

nonlinearities.shape: exponential decay in games played
nonlinearities.why: The survival probability of an undefeated start is a product of win probabilities and decays roughly exponentially with each game, with days clustering ties.
